sections.heading: Adding up what a delivery costs before you have a basket
sections.html:
Asda publishes the thresholds clearly and the slot prices barely at all. The thresholds are £40 for delivery and £25 for Click & Collect, and the penalty for coming in under either is a £4 minimum basket charge — a structure worth preferring to a hard refusal, because a £28 shop still gets delivered.

Two slot prices are published outright. Express delivery costs £8.50 to £8.99 and carries no minimum spend, which is the cheapest way to have a single forgotten item brought to the door of any service on this site; Asda's wording is “there is no minimum spend, we deliver as little as you need”. Express Click & Collect is £3.50 for the full range within four hours, with a 12 noon cut-off for collection after 4pm the same day. Ordinary booked slots are priced by day, time and store, and Asda does not put that table anywhere a shopper can read before signing in.

The Delivery Pass is the way round it. Passes start at £3.95 a month, a 12-month midweek pass is a single payment of £39.50 — about £3.29 a month — and Asda advertises savings of “up to £194 a year when you pay annually”. The conditions are tighter than the headline: the £40 minimum still applies, a pass covers up to one delivery a day, the midweek version works only on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday, and vouchers, coupons, eVouchers and gift cards cannot be used to buy one. Unused passes are refundable in full inside 14 days, and where a pass does not save what it promised Asda says it will “give you the difference in an eVoucher”, which is a real commitment rather than a slogan — though the arithmetic it is measured against is not published either.

For anyone shopping weekly, the sum is simple enough to do at the door. Fifty-two Express deliveries at £8.50 would be £442; the same year on a midweek pass is £39.50 plus the discipline of shopping on three named days.

sections.heading: The price claim, and the two baskets it depends on
sections.html:
Asda's central pitch is price, and for once there is independent daily measurement of it. Which? tracks 220 branded grocery lines every day for a month and averages the cost per item. In August 2026 that basket came to £771.27 at Asda, ahead of Tesco with a Clubcard at £782.39, Sainsbury's with Nectar at £787.57, Morrisons with a More card at £797.32, Ocado at £816.28 and Waitrose at £839.71. Strip the loyalty cards out and the gap widens sharply: Tesco at £860.29 is 11.54% dearer than Asda and Sainsbury's at £869.16 is 12.69% dearer. Asda's Q2 statement of 28 August 2026 says it has topped every Which? branded comparison since April and has retained The Grocer 33 annual pricing award.

The second basket is the one to read before switching. Which? also prices a mixed basket of 92 branded and own-label items across eight retailers, and in August 2026 Asda came third at £185.21, behind Aldi at £159.36 and Lidl at £161.10. That is £25.85 more than Aldi on one shop, about 16%. Both results are true and they answer different questions: Asda wins on the brands you asked for by name, and the discounters win once own-label is allowed in. Neither Aldi nor Lidl delivers a weekly grocery shop to the door, which is the reason the comparison is not quite like for like.

Behind the pricing sits a business under pressure. Asda's FY2025 update of 27 March 2026 reported sales excluding fuel of £21.0bn, down 3.3% from £21.7bn, like-for-like sales down 3.1%, and adjusted EBITDA after rent of £764m against £1.14bn the year before — a fall of 33.1%. Net debt came down by £500m to £3.1bn, with £1.3bn of cash and £2.1bn of liquidity. Store availability reached 95%, described as an eight-year high, which matters to an online shopper more than it sounds: availability is what decides how many substitutions land in the order. By Q2 2026 revenue including fuel was £6.5bn, up 0.4%, like-for-like still down 2.3%, and in the seven weeks to 18 August 2026 like-for-like sales excluding fuel turned positive at 0.2% — the first growth in more than two years, on Allan Leighton's account.

sections.heading: Substitutions, weights and the part that is not written down
sections.html:
The substitution rule is the best term on the service and it is stated in one line: “If something you have ordered is not available when we pick your order, we may choose a substitute. If it costs less, we charge you less. If it costs more, we won't charge you the extra.” A shopper who orders a £2 own-label and receives a £3.50 brand pays £2. Set against 95% availability, that turns the commonest annoyance of online grocery shopping into an occasional small windfall.

Loose goods work differently and the difference is worth a sentence. Fruit, vegetables and meat sold by weight are charged on what is actually weighed at picking, so those lines move in either direction against the basket total shown at checkout. Nothing about that is unusual, and it is the reason an Asda receipt rarely matches the order to the penny.

What is not published is how to refuse a substitute. Asda's own substitutions article says only that a substitute may be chosen and how it is priced; the mechanics — handing it back at the door, the refund route, how long the money takes — sit in help articles on support.asda.com, which refused every automated read attempted for this review. So did asda.com/terms/grocery, which is closed by robots rules, and groceries.asda.com, where product pages live. The delivery, Delivery Pass, Express and Click & Collect pages on asda.com all read normally, which is how the charges above were checked; the contract, the help centre and the product detail could not be. Anyone relying on a specific term should read it in the app before ordering rather than take it from a page like this one.

sections.heading: The use-by date is the one fact you cannot check before paying
sections.html:
In a shop you turn the pack over. Online you cannot, and the law is comfortable with that: the date of minimum durability is the particular an online grocer may leave until the moment of delivery rather than disclose before the sale is concluded. Which makes the accuracy of the printed date the whole of the protection, and that is measurable.

The governing rule is blunt. Article 14 of assimilated Regulation (EC) No 178/2002 says “food shall not be placed on the market if it is unsafe”, and food is unsafe if it is injurious to health or unfit for human consumption. Two of its paragraphs matter to a mislabelled pack in particular: paragraph 3 requires regard to “information provided to the consumer, including information on the label”, so the date is part of the safety assessment rather than a detail beside it; and paragraph 6 presumes that if one item in a batch is unsafe, the whole batch is, unless a detailed assessment shows otherwise. Separately, regulation 10 of the Food Information Regulations 2014 makes a failure to comply with the food information rules an offence, and regulation 12 pulls the Food Safety Act 1990's improvement notice machinery across to enforce it. The fine level on conviction could not be confirmed for this review — the relevant penalties regulation would not load — so it is left unstated rather than guessed.

Against that, Asda's record on the Food Standards Agency's register is specific and dated. Three Asda-brand products have been recalled since April 2024 for carrying the wrong date. The clearest is notice FSA-PRIN-52-2025 of 27 November 2025: Asda 10 Mini Duck Spring Rolls with Hoisin Dip, 220g, “labelled with an incorrect use by date of 29 December 2025 which makes them unsafe to consume after the correct use by date of 29 November 2025”. A month of life printed on a pack that had none, on a product a delivery customer had no way of inspecting before paying for it. Before that, FSA-PRIN-20-2025 of 29 April 2025 recalled ASDA Hot & Spicy Chicken Breast Slices and FSA-PRIN-16-2024 of 15 April 2024 recalled Asda Succulent Cooked & Peeled King Prawns, both for the same reason. Asda took all three back without a receipt.

How much life arrives with the shopping has been measured once, independently, and Asda came mid-table. Which? sent 12 shoppers to order 25 identical perishable items from six supermarkets between 27 March and 6 April 2023 — more than 1,700 groceries — and counted the hours left to midnight on the use-by date. Asda averaged 10.0 days, fourth behind Ocado on 11.2, Tesco on 10.2 and Morrisons on 10.1, and ahead of Waitrose on 9.9 and Sainsbury's on 9.7. One Asda order in that exercise contained stilton three days past its date. The research also settled a question a shopper might otherwise assume in Asda's favour: Asda lists a “typical life” against some products, and a typical life is not a guarantee of one. No supermarket in the exercise, Asda included, promised a minimum number of days on delivery. Which? has not repeated the study, so the 2023 ranking is the most recent independent measurement available and should be read as three years old.

sections.heading: Reading the recall register yourself, and what it will and will not tell you
sections.html:
The Food Standards Agency publishes every allergy alert, product recall notice and food alert for action as open data at data.food.gov.uk/food-alerts under the Open Government Licence, searchable by free text, alert type, allergen and date. A search on Asda returns dozens of notices going back to 2018, which is a larger number than it first appears to be and a smaller problem.

The reason is that most of them are not Asda's. Three Asda-brand recalls were posted in 2026 and only one began at Asda. FSA-PRIN-22-2026 of 30 April 2026 recalled Exceptional by ASDA Beer Battered Cod Fishcakes over possible plastic or metal pieces. FSA-PRIN-38-2026 of 7 August 2026 was Greencore's: three chilled pasta products over possible Listeria monocytogenes, of which two were Asda — the 300g Cheese & Tomato Pasta Salad with a use-by of 10 August 2026 and the 500g Nacho Cheese Pasta Salad with a use-by of 9 August — and the third was Morrisons'. FSA-PRIN-29-2026 of 23 June 2026 was Prepworld's, and it swept up 13 prepared fruit lines across six retailers over possible salmonella, with Asda's 220g Pink Lady Apple, Mango, Strawberry & Blueberry pot one of them alongside Morrisons, M&S, Sainsbury's, Tesco and Waitrose. A shared factory produces a shared recall, and reading a retailer's name count as a hygiene score gets that backwards.

The Listeria notice is worth one line of law because the number behind it is fixed. Under assimilated Regulation (EC) No 2073/2005, ready-to-eat food able to support the growth of Listeria monocytogenes must stay below 100 cfu/g through its shelf life on a plan of five samples with none permitted over the limit, and must be undetectable in 25g before it leaves the producer's control; for foods intended for infants or for special medical purposes the criterion is absence in 25g on ten samples. A chilled pasta salad is squarely in the growth-supporting category, which is why a use-by date on one is a safety instruction and not a suggestion.

One practical wrinkle for anyone ringing about a recall: the notices carry two different Asda numbers. The spring roll recall gives Customer Relations on 0800 952 0101 and the Greencore recall gives 0330 053 0111, and nothing published explains which line handles what.

sections.heading: Where a complaint goes when the customer service line says no
sections.html:
Groceries sit outside the ombudsman schemes that cover insurance, banking and energy, so the honest answer is that there is no free adjudicator for a shopper Asda has turned down. The nearest thing to a regulator in this market watches the other side of the till.

Asda Stores Ltd is one of the 14 retailers designated under the Groceries Supply Code of Practice and supervised by the Groceries Code Adjudicator. The statutory review of the Adjudicator published in April 2026, covering 1 April 2022 to 31 March 2025 after a consultation that ran from 13 May to 5 August 2025, records a mean compliance score across all designated retailers of 93% in 2025, 91% in 2024 and 92% in 2023, with every designated retailer above 90% in 2025 except Amazon on 66%. Asda is therefore in the upper band throughout, which is a reasonable proxy for how it treats the suppliers whose products end up in the delivery van. The Adjudicator completed three arbitrations and launched no new investigations in those three years, can fine a retailer up to 1% of all turnover, and ran on a levy of £2.2m in 2025/26. The Code protects suppliers, not households — a shopper cannot complain to it.

For the shopper the route is the ordinary one: Asda's own customer service, then the Consumer Rights Act through Trading Standards or the small claims court. Asda is not among the retailers listed by RetailADR, the Chartered Trading Standards Institute-approved dispute body, where roughly fifty merchants including Aldi, ASOS, IKEA and Richer Sounds do subscribe. Signing up is voluntary and most supermarkets have not, so this is a gap Asda shares with almost all of its competitors rather than one of its own making — but it is worth knowing that a stalled grocery dispute has nowhere cheap to go.

pros: Cheapest of eight supermarkets on Which?'s 220-item branded basket in August 2026 at £771.27, and Asda says it has topped that comparison every month since April
Substitutions can only reduce the bill: a cheaper swap is charged less and a dearer swap is not charged at all
Express delivery has no minimum spend whatsoever, at £8.50 to £8.99 within four hours and sometimes inside one
A £4 minimum basket charge instead of a flat refusal, so a shop under £40 still gets delivered
Midweek Delivery Pass at £39.50 for a year, roughly £3.29 a month, with a written promise of an eVoucher if the saving does not materialise
Store availability at 95%, an eight-year high, which is what decides how many substitutions reach the order
Orders can be amended until 11pm the night before the slot, and there are over 450 Click & Collect points
cons: Ordinary delivery slot prices are not published anywhere a shopper can read before creating an account and filling a basket. Only Express delivery (£8.50–£8.99) and Express Click & Collect (£3.50) carry printed prices.

The contract and the help centre could not be read for this review at all: asda.com/terms/grocery is closed by robots rules, and support.asda.com and groceries.asda.com both refused every request, so the substitution refusal route, refund timescales and product detail pages are unverifiable from outside the app.

Three Asda-brand products have been recalled since April 2024 for carrying an incorrect use-by date, and the November 2025 duck spring rolls were labelled a full month beyond the correct date — on exactly the fact an online customer cannot inspect before paying.

Asda lists a “typical life” on some products and it is not a guarantee. In the only independent measurement, Which?'s 2023 mystery shop, Asda came fourth of six on delivered shelf life at 10.0 days and one order contained stilton three days out of date. That study is three years old and has not been repeated.
The price win is narrower than the headline: on Which?'s mixed 92-item basket Asda was third in August 2026 at £185.21, some £25.85 or about 16% more than Aldi.

There is no dispute scheme to escalate to. Asda is not listed by RetailADR, so a refused complaint goes to Trading Standards or the small claims court, and the Groceries Code Adjudicator exists for suppliers rather than shoppers.
Two different Asda phone numbers appear on its 2025 and 2026 recall notices, 0800 952 0101 and 0330 053 0111, with nothing published to say which handles what.
verdict: On price, Asda is doing what it says: cheapest of the eight supermarkets Which? tracks on a 220-line branded basket in August 2026, and cheapest of the traditional supermarkets by its own 4–7% measure, with availability at an eight-year high and a substitution rule that can only ever move the bill down. For a household that buys brands by name and wants them delivered, that combination is hard to beat, and the £4 minimum basket charge is a kinder design than a flat £40 refusal. Two things temper it. Asda will not tell you what an ordinary slot costs until you are signed in and holding a basket, and the one fact a delivery customer cannot check — the date on the pack — is the fact three of its own recalls since April 2024 got wrong, once by a month. Read the “typical life” on a chilled line as an estimate rather than a promise, check the dates at the door while the driver is still there, and the economics work: a midweek pass at £39.50 a year against £8.50 a time pays for itself inside five shops.

faqs.q: What is the minimum spend for an Asda delivery?
faqs.a: £40 for a home delivery and £25 for Click & Collect. Asda does not refuse a smaller order; it applies a £4 minimum basket charge instead. Express delivery is the exception and has no minimum spend at all, at £8.50 to £8.99.

faqs.q: Is the Asda Delivery Pass worth buying?
faqs.a: It depends how often you order and on which days. Passes start at £3.95 a month and a 12-month midweek pass is £39.50, about £3.29 a month, covering Tuesday to Thursday only. Against Express delivery at £8.50 a time it pays for itself in about five shops a year. The £40 minimum still applies, a pass covers up to one delivery a day, and Asda will refund an unused pass in full within 14 days or pay the shortfall in an eVoucher if the advertised saving does not appear.

faqs.q: What happens if Asda substitutes an item I ordered?
faqs.a: You are charged the lower of the two prices. Asda's policy is that a cheaper substitute costs you less and a dearer substitute costs you nothing extra. Items sold by weight — fruit, vegetables, meat — are priced on the weight actually picked, so those lines can move a few pence either way. How to refuse a substitute at the door is set out in help articles that could not be read for this review, so check that in the app.

faqs.q: How much shelf life do Asda deliveries arrive with?
faqs.a: Asda does not publish a minimum. The “typical life” shown against some products is an estimate rather than a guarantee. The only independent measurement is Which?'s mystery shop of more than 1,700 perishable items between 27 March and 6 April 2023, in which Asda averaged 10.0 days of remaining life, fourth of six supermarkets behind Ocado at 11.2 days. Those figures are three years old.

faqs.q: Where can I check whether an Asda product has been recalled?
faqs.a: The Food Standards Agency publishes every recall and allergy alert as open data at data.food.gov.uk/food-alerts, searchable by free text and by date. Bear in mind that many notices naming Asda originate with a supplier and cover several supermarkets at once: the 23 June 2026 salmonella recall by Prepworld, for instance, covered 13 prepared fruit lines across six retailers.

faqs.q: Can I complain about Asda to an ombudsman?
faqs.a: No. Grocery retail has no ombudsman scheme, and Asda is not listed by RetailADR, the Chartered Trading Standards Institute-approved dispute body that Aldi and around fifty other merchants use. A complaint Asda refuses goes to Trading Standards or the small claims court under the Consumer Rights Act. The Groceries Code Adjudicator, which does supervise Asda, handles supplier complaints rather than customer ones.

title: ASOS Men's Fashion Review: Delivery, Returns and the 70% Return Rate
meta_title: ASOS Men's Fashion: Free Returns and the 70% Rule
meta_description: Free ASOS returns for account holders, 28 days from delivery, until your return rate hits 70%. Delivery prices, Premier and the £3.95 fair use fee.

headline.label: What a return costs when it does not fit
headline.value: Nothing for account holders, by Royal Mail drop-off or free collection, but £3.95 a parcel once your 12-month return rate passes 70% across 3 or more orders and you keep £40 or less of the order, and £3.95 on every guest return (checked 30 September 2026)

intro:
Sending a parcel back to ASOS costs an account holder nothing. You get 28 days from delivery, a Royal Mail Post Office or InPost drop-off, or a free Royal Mail collection that can be booked up to 5 days in advance, and the refund is aimed at within 14 days of the item reaching the warehouse. Standard delivery is £4.50 and free over £40; ASOS Premier is £9.95 for 12 months. Every figure on this page was checked on 30 September 2026 against ASOS's own customer care pages, its annual report and the Competition and Markets Authority's case file.

One change is worth knowing before you fill a basket. Since January 2026 free returns are conditional on a personal return rate: if you have returned more than 70% of the value of your orders over the past 12 months and placed 3 or more orders, ASOS may deduct and retain £3.95 from your refund for each returned parcel, unless you keep more than £40 of that order. The rate is calculated on value rather than item count, it updates every time you order, changes to your status carry a 30-day delay, and it is shown to you in the app and at checkout before you commit. Guest checkout is charged the £3.95 on every return regardless.

What you are shopping is one of the largest menswear ranges in the country, and the company behind it is mid-turnaround rather than mid-collapse. ASOS had 16.5m active customers across more than 150 markets at its half year to 1 March 2026, an average basket of £44.43, about 10 own-brand labels running at roughly 40% of gross merchandise value, and around 150 brands inside its flexible fulfilment model. Menswear is being narrowed on purpose: the interim statement describes it as "more targeted as we rebuild momentum, emphasising functional fashion delivered with a clear styling edge rather than broad, generalist positioning".

sections.heading: The delivery ladder, and where Premier pays for itself
sections.html:
ASOS prices UK delivery in seven ways and publishes all of them. Standard Delivery is £4.50 and takes 3 to 4 business days, free once the order passes £40. Next Day Delivery is £5.95 and arrives between 7am and 10pm on the next working day. Nominated Day, which lets you pick a date up to 10 days ahead, is also £5.95. Click & Collect mirrors the same two prices through Royal Mail, at £4.50 standard or £5.95 next day. At the top, ASOS Instant costs £9.95 for an evening slot between 6pm and 10pm in London, and ASOS Instant AM with DPD costs £9.95 for delivery before 12 noon the next day.

Against that, ASOS Premier is £9.95 for a 12-month subscription, which is the price of a single Instant delivery. It gives free Standard Delivery with no minimum spend at all, and free Next Day and Nominated Day Delivery on orders over £15 after any discount is applied. Two Next Day orders in a year cover the cost. The exclusions are geographic and specific: Next Day and Nominated Day are unavailable in the Channel Islands and in the postcode areas AB31 to AB56, BF, FK, HS, IM, IV, KA27 to KA28, KW, PA20 to PA80, PH15 to PH50, TR21 to TR25 and ZE, where Standard Delivery still runs. The refund position is narrow and stated plainly in ASOS's own wording: you can get your money back only if you have made no eligible purchase within one calendar month, and otherwise "we won't be able to offer you a refund".

Students get 10% off, verified through SheerID with UniDAYS, Student Beans, TOTUM and Apprentice extra codes accepted as alternatives. It applies to students over 16 in full-time or part-time education, including apprenticeships, across 17 markets including the UK and Ireland, and it requires an account rather than a guest checkout.

sections.heading: The 70% line, and the arithmetic sitting behind it
sections.html:
This is the figure that now decides what ASOS costs a menswear shopper, because clothes are the one category where trying two sizes and sending one back is normal behaviour rather than indecision. ASOS's fair use policy sets two thresholds, and both are expressed in value, not items.

At a return rate above 70% across 3 or more orders in the past 12 months, ASOS "may deduct and retain £3.95 from your refund for each returned parcel (unless you keep more than £40 of your order)". At a return rate above 80% across 5 or more orders, the same £3.95 deduction applies and ASOS additionally adds "an additional £3.95 handling fee to your orders, in addition to our usual delivery costs". So the worst case on a single order is £3.95 charged going out and £3.95 withheld coming back, on top of whatever the delivery cost, and none of it is a postage charge as such.

Two details make this fairer than it first sounds. The rate is assessed over a rolling 12 months and recalculated every time you place an order, with a deliberate 30-day delay before your status changes, so one bad month does not flip you instantly. And ASOS tells you where you stand rather than surprising you: notification of a status change, a reminder at checkout before you order, and a further reminder when you set up the return. Since early 2026 the app also shows your personal return rate as a running figure, calculated from the value of what you have sent back against the value of what you have ordered over 12 months. A retailer publishing the number it is about to charge you on is unusual, and it is the single most useful thing on the ASOS account page for anyone who buys trousers in two waist sizes.

The threshold also reaches beyond the fee. A return rate of 70% or more across 3 or more orders blocks you from buying or renewing ASOS Premier at all. And from January 2026 the same 70% line gates the loyalty scheme: ASOS.WORLD runs four tiers, Stylist free to join, Curator at £100 of spend, Icon at £350 and A-Lister at £750, with the 12-month spend assessment excluding returned or cancelled orders, and progress to the upper tiers requiring a return rate below 70%. Returning something after a tier upgrade deducts the refunded amount from your progress, and a downgrade lands within about 60 minutes of the refund being processed.

sections.heading: Why ASOS is counting returns: the figures in its own accounts
sections.html:
The returns policy is not a pricing whim, and the published numbers make that clear. In the 52 weeks to 31 August 2025, ASOS reported revenue of £2,477.8m, down 15% year on year, with UK revenue of £1,211.8m, down 9%. Active customers fell 14% to 17.0m and shipped orders fell 16% to 57.3m, while the average basket rose 3% to £42.89. The profitability side moved the other way: adjusted gross margin improved 370 basis points to 47.1%, adjusted EBITDA came in at £131.6m on a margin up 250 basis points to 5.3%, the adjusted loss before tax narrowed to £98.2m from £126.0m, and net debt improved by £112.4m to £184.7m.

The interim results published on 23 April 2026, covering the 26 weeks to 1 March 2026, continued that shape. Revenue was £1,116.0m, down 14%, with UK revenue down 12%. Adjusted gross margin reached 48.5%, up 330 basis points. Adjusted EBITDA rose 51%, or £21.5m, to £64.0m, though the reported loss before tax was £137.9m against an adjusted loss of £52.4m, and net debt excluding lease liabilities stood at £294.9m. Active customers were 16.5m, orders 26.3m, and the average basket £44.43. Guidance for the full year, set out in the 25 March 2026 pre-close statement, is adjusted EBITDA of £150m to £180m, a gross margin of 48% to 50%, and broadly neutral free cash flow. The full-year figures for the period that has just ended are not published yet.

Inside those numbers sits the sentence that explains the policy: the underlying returns rate improved by about 160 basis points year on year in the half, which ASOS attributes to sizing and fit work plus the transparency initiative launched in early 2026. Sales are falling and margin is rising, and a large part of the margin is coming from fewer parcels going backwards. The supporting machinery has shrunk to match: around 2,800 employees, three distribution centres at Barnsley, Berlin and a returns facility in Dallas, a warehouse footprint cut by more than half since 2021, and stock down to about £400m, roughly 20% lower year on year and about 60% below the 2022 peak. The Test & React model, which puts small batches into production and repeats only what sells, passed 20% of own-brand sales in the year to August 2025, grew a further 6 percentage points in the half, and is targeted at 30% in the medium term. Buying less of the wrong thing and selling more of it at full price is the whole strategy, and the returns fee is the consumer-facing edge of it.

sections.heading: The green claims ASOS had to rewrite, and the clock running on them
sections.html:
ASOS is one of only three fashion businesses to have given the Competition and Markets Authority formal undertakings over environmental claims, and the documents are public, which makes this the most closely specified part of its sales copy. The investigation opened on 29 July 2022 and closed on 27 March 2024 when the CMA accepted undertakings from ASOS, Boohoo and George at Asda, three businesses accounting for about £4.4bn of annual UK fashion sales between them. The range at the centre of the ASOS case was the Responsible edit. Sarah Cardell, the CMA's chief executive, said that "following our action, the millions of people who shop with these well-known businesses can now have confidence in the green claims they see".

The undertaking itself was given under Part 8 of the Enterprise Act 2002, on the section 219 route, in relation to the Consumer Protection from Unfair Trading Regulations 2008, and its operative paragraphs are more precise than the press release. Paragraph 19 requires that where a product is described as containing recycled or organic fibres, ASOS must clearly and prominently set out either the specific percentage evidenced through its supplier due diligence, or the minimum percentage the product must contain. Paragraph 18 bars a recycled or organic claim where the product contains fibres that are not, unless the non-qualifying proportion is negligible. Paragraph 7 requires the criteria for any environmental range to be shown clearly and prominently in an easily identifiable and accessible location. Paragraph 6 bars filter names that would themselves amount to a misleading environmental claim, and paragraph 10 requires fabric inclusion to rest on objective characteristics rather than a subjective or ambiguous label such as "eco-fabrics". On reporting, paragraph 35 requires compliance reports within 20 working days of the end of each reporting period, and paragraph 40 requires spot check reports within 10 working days of the end of each spot check period, those periods running every 3 months.

The duration clause is where a shopper should pay attention. The undertaking runs to a reporting end date defined as the later of two years from the date of the undertaking, or two years from the launch of an ASOS New Range, meaning a successor to the Responsible edit launched within two years. The CMA's case page refers to the Responsible edit in the past tense, and no environmental product range is currently visible on the ASOS site. On the first limb, the two-year clock from 27 March 2024 would have run out on 27 March 2026. Whether the CMA still treats the reporting obligation as live, and whether ASOS has launched a qualifying new range, could not be established from any published source and needs confirming with the CMA rather than assuming either way. The same day, the CMA also wrote an open letter to the whole fashion sector setting out six principles for environmental claims, and pointed at the penalties then coming through the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Bill, which reach up to 10% of a business's worldwide turnover.

Worth stating for balance: ASOS's own reporting says 50% of the materials in its own-brand ranges were sustainable materials in the year to August 2025, against a target of 45%. That is a company-level figure and not a product claim, which is exactly the distinction the undertaking was written to force.

sections.heading: Who you are buying from, and who handles it when the parcel is wrong
sections.html:
Not every item on the site is sold by ASOS, and the difference matters most at the point you want to send something back. Items shipped by ASOS Brand Partners are returned under that brand's own policy, applied at the brand's discretion, so the 28-day window and the free Royal Mail route are not site-wide guarantees. Some partner lines are handled separately again, with New Balance having its own named returns article. Payment is affected too: American Express cannot be used on an order sold and shipped by a Brand Partner, though Visa, Mastercard, Google Pay, Apple Pay, PayPal, Clearpay, Klarna and the ASOS Credit Card are all accepted elsewhere, and ASOS notes that some payment methods are subject to a soft credit check. Orders can also be split across warehouses, which is why a single order can arrive as several parcels with different return routes attached.

The legal identity behind the checkout is ASOS.com Limited, company number 03584121, at Greater London House, Hampstead Road, London NW1 7FB, with ASOS Payments UK Limited, company number 13337408, handling payments. ASOS's own terms give a 14-day cancellation right from delivery or availability for collection under the Consumer Contracts (Information, Cancellation and Additional Charges) Regulations 2013, so the 28-day returns window is double the statutory minimum. On pricing mistakes the terms are explicit rather than weaselly: if an error is discovered, ASOS says it will tell you as soon as possible and give you the option of reconfirming at the correct price or cancelling.

If a complaint is not resolved, ASOS is a listed member of RetailADR, the retail alternative dispute resolution scheme run by Consumer Dispute Resolution Ltd, company number 09189773. That is a genuine point of difference: most large UK retailers, supermarkets included, have not subscribed to any ADR scheme, and retail has no ombudsman, so an unresolved dispute elsewhere ends at Trading Standards or the small claims court. Note also the limit of the fair use fee that Which? has pointed out: under the Consumer Rights Act 2015 you cannot be charged for returning goods that are faulty, of poor quality or not as described, whatever your return rate, so a fee applied to a faulty item is not lawful and should be challenged rather than absorbed.

On product safety, the Office for Product Safety and Standards register of alerts, reports and recalls returns 0 results for the keyword "asos", checked on 30 September 2026. That is an absence rather than an award, but it is an absence worth having in a category where the same register carries 248 entries for clothing and 135 for textiles.

sections.heading: The supply chain ASOS publishes, and the parts it does not
sections.html:
ASOS's modern slavery statement for September 2024 to August 2025 was approved by the board on 28 October 2025 and signed by chief executive José Antonio Ramos, and it is more numerate than most. It records 441 active factories in Tiers 1 and 2 across 21 countries, covering approximately 236,750 workers through 164 suppliers, with a workforce split of 49.87% male and 50.13% female. It maps five tiers, from finished manufacturing down to raw materials, and states visibility through Tier 2, which means subcontracted manufacturing sites are in scope and fabric mills, component makers and raw material suppliers largely are not. On grievances it reports 33 whistleblowing cases received, of which 26 have been resolved, with investigations continuing on the rest.

The gaps are stated in the document rather than hidden. It names unannounced and semi-unannounced audits and its audit partners without publishing the number of audits carried out or a breakdown of findings, so there is no way to judge how often something is found. Training distribution is given as 53 suppliers in China without a count of workers reached. And due diligence on goods not for resale is described as an area where work continues. A factory count, a country count and a worker count are real disclosure; an audit count with results attached would be better, and it is the figure a reader would actually use.

pros: Returns cost account holders nothing in the ordinary case: 28 days from delivery, Royal Mail Post Office or 24/7 InPost drop-off, or a free Royal Mail collection bookable up to 5 days ahead
28-day returns window is double the 14-day statutory cancellation right
ASOS Premier is £9.95 for 12 months and covers free Standard Delivery with no minimum spend, so two Next Day orders at £5.95 pay for it
Your personal return rate is shown in the app and at checkout before you order, so the £3.95 deduction is never a surprise
Standard delivery free over £40, with a published seven-option delivery ladder from £4.50 to £9.95
ASOS is one of roughly fifty retailers signed up to RetailADR, which most large UK retailers are not
Zero entries on the OPSS product safety alerts and recalls register for ASOS, checked 30 September 2026
10% student discount, verified through SheerID with UniDAYS, Student Beans and TOTUM accepted
Free DPD ReLove charity collection of unwanted clothing alongside a delivery, with Scope, Marie Curie, British Heart Foundation, British Red Cross and The Children's Society as the named charities
Supply chain disclosure is specific: 441 factories, 21 countries, 164 suppliers and roughly 236,750 workers named in figures
cons: The £40 keep-threshold cuts the wrong way for small baskets: above a 70% return rate, sending back a single £35 shirt costs £3.95, while keeping £41 of a £300 order costs nothing

Above an 80% return rate across 5 or more orders the charge doubles up, with £3.95 withheld from the refund on each returned parcel and a further £3.95 handling fee added to the order on top of normal delivery

One number triggers three separate penalties: passing 70% across 3 or more orders brings the return deduction, blocks buying or renewing Premier at £9.95, and from January 2026 blocks progress to the Icon and A-Lister tiers of ASOS.WORLD
Guest checkout is charged £3.95 on every return however little is sent back, so the cheapest way to try two sizes is to hand over your details

Brand Partner items are returned under the partner's own policy at the partner's discretion, so the 28-day window and the free return route are not site-wide, and American Express is refused on those orders
A refund can take up to 10 calendar days for the parcel to be processed and then up to 10 working days to clear, which is 4 weeks in the worst case on money you have already paid
No product price could be read from asos.com on any fetch, so no like-for-like cheapest-item comparison with other menswear retailers is possible from published sources

There is no independent customer satisfaction score for a menswear retailer to set against any of this: Which? publishes rated best-and-worst-shops surveys for baby shops, technology and furniture, and none for clothing

The Responsible edit has gone and no successor environmental range is visible on the site, leaving it unclear whether the CMA reporting obligation, whose first limb expired on 27 March 2026, still binds anything
The modern slavery statement gives factory and worker counts but no number of audits carried out and no breakdown of findings, so the depth of the checking cannot be judged
verdict: For a menswear shopper who buys, keeps most of it and sends the odd thing back, ASOS is close to the cheapest large retailer to deal with: nothing to return within 28 days, free standard delivery over £40, and £9.95 a year for Premier removing the delivery question entirely. The catch is aimed squarely at the other kind of customer. Once your 12-month return rate passes 70% across 3 or more orders, £3.95 goes per returned parcel unless you keep more than £40 of the order, Premier is closed to you, and the upper loyalty tiers are closed too; above 80% across 5 orders a second £3.95 is added on the way out. Whether that matters to you is a question you can actually answer before you order, because the rate is on the account page, and that is more than most retailers charging for returns will tell you. Check it, then decide whether to order two sizes or one.

faqs.q: Is it free to return something to ASOS in the UK?
faqs.a: For an account holder in the ordinary case, yes. You have 28 days from delivery, you can drop the parcel at a Royal Mail Post Office or an InPost locker or shop, or book a free Royal Mail collection up to 5 days in advance Monday to Saturday. Two situations are charged: a guest checkout order always has £3.95 deducted from the refund, and an account whose return rate has passed 70% of order value across 3 or more orders in the past 12 months has £3.95 deducted per returned parcel unless more than £40 of that order is kept.

faqs.q: How does ASOS work out my return rate, and can I see it?
faqs.a: It compares the value of what you have returned with the value of what you have ordered over the past 12 months, so it is a value measure rather than a count of items. It is recalculated every time you place an order, and any change to your status is held for 30 days before it takes effect. Since early 2026 the figure is shown to you in the app, and you also get reminders at checkout and again when you create a return.

faqs.q: Is ASOS Premier worth £9.95?
faqs.a: Arithmetically, if you place two or more orders a year that you would otherwise pay to deliver. Premier costs £9.95 for 12 months and gives free Standard Delivery with no minimum spend, plus free Next Day and Nominated Day Delivery on orders over £15 after discounts, against £4.50 and £5.95 respectively without it. Next Day and Nominated Day are excluded in the Channel Islands and a long list of Scottish and island postcode areas. It does not cover returns, and if your return rate is 70% or higher across 3 or more orders you cannot buy or renew it at all.

faqs.q: Can ASOS charge me £3.95 for returning something faulty?
faqs.a: No. Under the Consumer Rights Act 2015 you cannot be charged for returning goods that are faulty, of poor quality or not as described, and that applies regardless of your return rate, as Which? set out when the policy changed in January 2026. If a deduction is taken on a faulty item, raise it with customer care and, if it is not put right, take it to RetailADR, the alternative dispute resolution scheme ASOS is a member of.

faqs.q: Am I buying from ASOS or from another brand?
faqs.a: Both, depending on the item. Own-brand labels are about 40% of gross merchandise value across roughly 10 brands, with partner brands making up the rest and around 150 brands inside the flexible fulfilment model. Items sold and shipped by an ASOS Brand Partner are returned under that brand's policy at its discretion rather than under the 28-day ASOS policy, and American Express is not accepted on those orders. An order can also ship from more than one warehouse, so check which route each parcel takes before sending anything back.

title: ASOS Women's Fashion: Vintage Boutiques, Resale and the Jewellery Small Print
meta_title: ASOS Women's Fashion: Vintage Boutiques and Resale
meta_description: ASOS vintage runs to 1,012 tops and 537 dresses from boutiques like 28 Vintage, from GBP 21.60. What resale pays, and the jewellery wording the law dictates.
intro:
ASOS put 51 adaptive pieces on sale on 24 September 2026, priced £32 to £65 and cut in XS to 3XL, co-created with Disabled customers and the accessibility consultancy Tilting the Lens. Magnetic fastenings, hidden zips, tube access points, contoured waistbands proportioned for seated wearers, shortened jacket lengths. Figures taken from ASOS's own announcement and checked on 1 October 2026.

That is the newest thing on the womenswear side of the site, and it is worth knowing before anything else, because it is the sort of range a buyer only gets from a retailer with 2,310 jewellery styles and several thousand clothing lines to spread a risk across. The second thing worth knowing is where the second-hand clothes are. ASOS sells genuine vintage — 1,012 vintage tops and 537 vintage dresses as at 1 October 2026, from £21.60 to £189.00 — but not one piece of it is ASOS's own stock. Every item belongs to an independent boutique trading on ASOS's pages, which means your contract is with the boutique and so is the returns policy.

And ASOS will not buy your clothes back. The route out is a separate company, Thrift+, which pays between 10% and 40% of what your clothes fetch, and that is covered in full below.

sections.heading: The vintage rail is real, and it belongs to somebody else
sections.html:
ASOS ran a separate site for independent sellers for years. On 23 January 2025 it announced that the vintage and boutique sellers on it would move onto asos.com itself, and the migration was set to finish by April 2025. The sellers landed inside what ASOS calls Partner Fulfils, part of its flexible fulfilment arrangement, where the boutique holds its own stock and posts the parcel itself. Shazmeen Malik, then Brands Director, framed it as curation rather than consolidation. The old address has simply stopped being a shop: a request to marketplace.asos.com on 1 October 2026 answers with a 302 redirect to the main site and nothing else.

What survived the move is better than the phrase suggests. Women's Vintage on asos.com is broken out into New In, Accessories & Jewellery, Tops, Dresses, Skirts, Jeans, Trousers & Shorts, Coats & Jackets, Jumpers & Cardigans and Sale. The tops category alone returns 1,012 styles and dresses 537. The boutiques are named on every listing — 28 Vintage, Second Wave Vintage, Messina Hembry, Christie's Cupboard, Blank Seams, Remass, Atlas Vintage, Old But Gold Vintage, Jarlia by Jolina — and the stock ranges from £21.60 for an unbranded woven mini dress up to £189.00 for an 80s Yves Saint Laurent giraffe-print belt-waist dress. A 90s Balenciaga velvet dress and a 90s Yohji Yamamoto wool dress were both listed at £175.44 on the day this page was written.

One practical note that matters more than it sounds. Prices on these vintage pages are plainly readable, item by item, which is not true of every ASOS landing page. If you want to know what second-hand actually costs here before you commit to anything, the category pages will tell you.

sections.heading: Sending clothes the other way, and what the 20% band really means
sections.html:
ASOS has had a resale route since 6 June 2022, when it launched its second circular design collection — over 40 pieces using Texloop RCOT and TENCEL Refibra, with the denim built to the Ellen MacArthur Foundation's Jeans Redesign requirements, including 100% pre-consumer recycled materials and a design life of 30 or more home washes — and a trial partnership with Thrift+ alongside it. The trial opened with 30,000 free bags. Vanessa Spence, then Commercial Design and Visual Director, put it plainly: design is one piece of the circular puzzle, and products have to pass through circular systems too.

The scheme still runs as ASOS X Thrift+. You order a free bag, fill it with pre-owned clothing, shoes and accessories across high street, premium and designer brands, and send it back at no cost. Thrift+ photographs, lists and sells the items, and you earn credit when they sell. The rates are published: 10% of the sale price on anything that sells for £4.99 or less, 20% from £5 to £49.99, and 40% above £50. Sellers can opt into real cash instead of credit, paid monthly once the balance reaches £5.00, though credits already earned cannot be converted retrospectively. Anything unsuitable for resale is passed to charity shops or recycled, and it is not sent back.

Do the arithmetic before you fill the bag. A dress that resells at £20 sits in the 20% band and returns £4 to the person who wore it. A £4 top returns 40p. That is not a criticism of the rate so much as a description of what the labour of sorting, shooting, storing and posting somebody else's wardrobe costs; it is simply worth knowing in advance rather than after. There is a visible market for it at the ASOS end: 450 pre-owned ASOS-brand women's items were listed on Thrift+ on 1 October 2026.

sections.heading: Why a £6 pair of silver hoops carries no hallmark
sections.html:
The jewellery pages are where the legal wording gets interesting, and it is worth understanding because it explains a pattern that otherwise looks evasive. Under the Hallmarking Act 1973 it is an offence to describe an article, in the course of a business, as made wholly or partly of gold, silver, platinum or palladium unless it carries a hallmark. The Act bites on the description, not on the metal. So a retailer that writes gold tone, silver tone, 18k plated, 14k gold plated or waterproof stainless steel is not dodging anything — it is staying outside a statute that would otherwise require every piece to go through an assay office.

Across 2,310 women's jewellery styles at £5.00 to £85.00, that plated and tone wording is what ASOS's own-brand and partner listings mostly use: ASOS DESIGN, DesignB London, Pieces, Accessorize, Topshop, My Accessories, Bershka, Pull&Bear, Reclaimed Vintage, Lost Souls, D. LOUISE and Kingsley Ryan. Where a listing does claim precious metal it says so flatly — a search for sterling silver returns 240 styles from £4.00 to £255.00, including Kingsley Ryan 10mm twisted hoops in sterling silver at £6.00, a Lovisa open ring at £19.50, a Thomas Sabo chain necklace in 925 sterling silver at £50.00 and a Lauren Ralph Lauren teardrop pendant at £115.00.

Now the weights, because they decide which of those has to be marked. An article needs no UK hallmark below 1g for gold, 7.78g for silver, 0.5g for platinum or 1g for palladium. A pair of 10mm twisted hoops is comfortably under 7.78g, so a £6.00 sterling silver earring can be described as silver, sold as silver and carry no mark whatever, entirely lawfully. A £100 Thomas Sabo bracelet almost certainly is not under it, and should be marked. The compulsory marks are three: the sponsor's mark showing who submitted the article, the assay office mark showing where it was tested, and the fineness mark. Date letters and pictorial town marks are optional extras. Trading Standards enforces all of it.

sections.heading: Vintage gold, the 1950 line, and whose job it is to prove it
sections.html:
This is where the two halves of the page meet. Old jewellery frequently carries no hallmark, and the law makes room for that: an article manufactured before 1950 may be described and sold as precious metal without a hallmark, provided the seller can show it is of minimum fineness and that it has had no improper alteration since 1950. The fineness floors for the exemption are 375 parts per thousand for gold and 800 for silver. Platinum articles made before 1 January 1975 are exempt, and palladium before 1 January 2010, which is the year palladium was brought into the hallmarking regime at all. Several narrower pre-1975 categories also sit outside it, including certain rings, filigree work and jeweller's settings.

Read that against how ASOS's vintage pages are structured and the practical point is obvious. The burden of proving the date and the fineness falls on the seller. On a vintage listing, the seller is the boutique. ASOS's own terms are unambiguous about this: where goods are sold and shipped by an ASOS Brand Partner, you enter into a contract to buy with that partner, and your contract with ASOS Payments UK Limited covers only the payment. Where an item is sold by a partner but shipped by ASOS, ASOS.com Limited (company number 3584121) is the seller. So if you are buying a £180 vintage gold chain described as gold, the firm that has to stand behind that description is whichever boutique's name sits on the listing, and the question to ask before paying is which it is.

The returns mechanics follow the same split and are more generous than you might expect. Brand Partner returns are free and go direct to the brand rather than to ASOS, with up to 10 calendar days for the parcel to be received and processed and up to 15 for some brands. Sending one to ASOS instead delays the refund. The policies themselves, though, are at each brand's discretion rather than set centrally, which on a one-of-a-kind item is the part worth reading first.

sections.heading: The notice that should be on the page, and was not
sections.html:
There is a second hallmarking duty, and it is the one with a visible gap. Anyone dealing in precious metals must display an approved Dealer's Notice, explaining the marks and the exemption weights, in a conspicuous position. The current version became compulsory on 1 May 2020, issued by the British Hallmarking Council, which supervises the four UK assay offices. The format is prescribed: printed in black and white, clearly legible, A4 portrait at 210mm x 297mm or larger, reproduced in its entirety with no amendments, additions or deletions. The 2020 revision added a differentiated Birmingham mark for articles marked outside the UK — a vertical anchor and compass in a cut-cornered rectangle, mandatory since 1 April 2019 — and a generic type 2 Convention conformity mark.

The Council's published position is that the Act reaches internet sales and that premises includes a website, so dealers supplying precious metal articles online should carry the notice on the site. Searching ASOS's terms and conditions and its customer care index on 1 October 2026 turned up no Dealer's Notice and no statement about precious metals, fineness or hallmarks anywhere. That is an absence found in the two places a reader would look, and it is reported as exactly that rather than as a finding: a large site has many pages, the duty's application to a general retailer selling mostly plated jewellery is not something this page can settle, and a question for ASOS or for Trading Standards is the honest next step. It needs confirming.

One more piece of wording deserves a mention while we are on the subject of what labels promise. Reclaimed Vintage is an ASOS house brand, sold under the ASOS Brands heading for both women and men, and it is new clothing rather than second-hand. Its brand page carries navigation and no explanation at all of what is reclaimed or vintage about it. Shoppers looking for actual old clothes want the Vintage category and the boutiques in it, not this.

sections.heading: What the recall register shows about the names on these listings
sections.html:
The Office for Product Safety and Standards publishes every alert, report and recall, and jewellery is a recurring entry: a search of the register on 1 October 2026 returns 69 jewellery reports. Nickel is the dominant hazard, because nickel in prolonged skin contact is a sensitiser and the limits are low.

One of those reports concerns a brand that ASOS sells. Product safety report 2512-0348, published 9 January 2026, covers the Lost Souls 'S' Initial Necklace — gold-coloured necklaces with S-shaped pendants, identifier 152384001, country of origin China. The nickel content exceeded the maximum permissible limit, the risk was recorded as serious chemical, the breach was recorded against the REACH Enforcement Regulations 2008, it was notified by local authority Trading Standards, and the affected products were destroyed. Lost Souls appears as a brand on ASOS's women's jewellery pages. Two things need saying with that. The report does not name ASOS, and it concerns a specific consignment rather than a retailer's stock — a destroyed consignment is the system working, not a product on sale. But a shopper filtering 2,310 pieces of inexpensive jewellery has no way of telling which brands have ever been caught by the register, and that is the useful thing to know.

The same register also carries MISSOMA stud earrings (2509-0310, 17 October 2025, recalled from end users) and a Bees Jewellery hand chain, bangle and earrings (2601-0411, 3 February 2026, destroyed). Checked directly against the register on 1 October 2026, the keyword asos itself returns nothing.

sections.heading: Who actually owns the brands in your basket
sections.html:
Topshop sits in the brand list on ASOS's women's jewellery pages and across its clothing, and most shoppers assume ASOS owns it. It mostly does not. On 5 September 2024 ASOS announced a joint venture in which Heartland — the Holch Povlsen family's business, which also owns Bestseller, with more than £4bn of sales across its channels and around 2,800 retail stores in over 30 countries — took 75% of Topshop and Topman for £135m in cash, valuing the two brands at £180m. ASOS Holdings Limited kept 25%. Net consideration to ASOS was expected at roughly £118m after fees and Nordstrom's pro-rata share, and the deal was guided to knock £10m to £20m off FY25 EBITDA before becoming accretive.

What ASOS kept is the part that affects a shopper. It holds design and distribution rights for both brands and pays royalties to go on marketing and selling them online, with exclusive wholesale distribution rights in the UK and North America, and it said at the time that it intended to relaunch Topshop.com within six months of completion. So buying Topshop on ASOS is buying a brand ASOS designs and distributes under licence and owns a quarter of. Nothing about that is hidden, and nothing about it changes your consumer rights, which run against the seller named on the listing exactly as they do on any other item. It is simply not what the brand name implies.

ASOS's own financial year ended on 31 August 2026 and the full-year results had not been published when this page was written, with the latest releases on its corporate site running to an Adaptive collection on 24 September 2026, a creative partnership with stylist Law Roach on 19 September and a London Fashion Week event on 18 September. Anyone weighing up how long a boutique's listing or a loyalty balance is likely to last should read those results when they land rather than relying on this page for it.

pros: 51 adaptive pieces launched 24 September 2026 at £32 to £65 in XS to 3XL, co-created with Disabled customers and Tilting the Lens, with magnetic fastenings, tube access points and waistbands proportioned for seated wearers
Genuine designer vintage at boutique prices — 1,012 vintage tops and 537 vintage dresses, from £21.60 for unbranded pieces to £189.00 for 80s Yves Saint Laurent
Every vintage boutique is named on the listing, so you can see who you are buying from before you pay
Returns on Brand Partner items are free, and vintage category pages show individual prices plainly
A working route to resell your own clothes through ASOS X Thrift+, with a free bag and free return postage, and an option to take real cash monthly once the balance passes £5.00
240 jewellery styles described as sterling silver, starting at £4.00, alongside 2,310 styles overall from £5.00
cons: ASOS holds no pre-owned stock of its own. Every second-hand item is an independent boutique's, your contract is with that boutique, and its returns policy is at its own discretion rather than set by ASOS — which on a one-of-a-kind garment is the policy that matters most

Resale pays the owner 10% of anything selling at £4.99 or less and 20% up to £49.99, so a dress that resells for £20 returns £4; credits earned before opting into cash payouts cannot be converted; and items judged unsuitable for resale are donated or recycled and never returned

The ASOS voucher named as a payout option in the June 2022 launch release is no longer stated on the current partnership page, which lists only Thrift+ store credit or a charity donation (checked 1 October 2026)

Material wording across 2,310 jewellery styles is as thin as gold tone, silver tone and 18k plated, with no fineness stated on the listings — lawful, because the Hallmarking Act bites on the description, but it leaves a shopper unable to tell plated base metal from anything else

No hallmarking Dealer's Notice could be found on asos.com's terms or customer care pages, although the British Hallmarking Council's position is that a website counts as premises for the purpose — this needs confirming with ASOS rather than assuming either way
Reclaimed Vintage is an ASOS house brand of new clothing whose brand page offers no explanation of what is reclaimed or vintage about it

On a pre-1950 vintage piece described as gold or silver, the duty to prove the date and the fineness falls on the boutique, and ASOS does not publish any requirement that its vintage partners hold that evidence
verdict: As a womenswear retailer ASOS is doing something few of its size bother with: 51 adaptive pieces at £32 to £65 in XS to 3XL, co-created rather than consulted on, is a real range rather than a gesture. On the second-hand question that this category is compared on, the answer is better than the brand's reputation suggests and more complicated than its pages admit. There is genuine vintage here — 1,012 tops, 537 dresses, 80s Yves Saint Laurent next to £21.60 unbranded — but it is boutique stock sold through ASOS, with boutique returns policies, and marketplace.asos.com now just redirects to the front page. Selling your own clothes means a third party, Thrift+, and a 20% band that turns a £20 dress into £4. The jewellery is where to read carefully: 2,310 styles of gold tone and plated, 240 described as sterling silver, and a 7.78g exemption that lawfully lets a £6 silver hoop carry no mark at all. Worth buying from, with the boutique's name and the metal wording checked first.

faqs.q: Does ASOS sell second-hand clothes?
faqs.a: Yes, but none of it is ASOS's own stock. Women's Vintage on asos.com carried 1,012 tops and 537 dresses on 1 October 2026, priced from £21.60 to £189.00, all of it held and posted by independent boutiques such as 28 Vintage, Second Wave Vintage and Messina Hembry. The separate marketplace.asos.com site closed after a migration announced on 23 January 2025 and completed by April 2025, and the address now returns a 302 redirect to the main site.

faqs.q: Can I sell my old clothes to ASOS?
faqs.a: Not to ASOS. The route is ASOS X Thrift+, launched with 30,000 free bags on 6 June 2022 and still running. You fill a free bag, return it at no cost, and earn 10% of the sale price on items selling at £4.99 or less, 20% from £5 to £49.99 and 40% above £50. You can opt to take cash monthly once your balance passes £5.00, but credits earned before opting in cannot be converted. Items unsuitable for resale go to charity shops or recycling and are not returned.

faqs.q: Why does ASOS jewellery say gold tone instead of gold?
faqs.a: Because of the Hallmarking Act 1973. Describing an article in trade as made of gold, silver, platinum or palladium without a hallmark is an offence, so wording such as gold tone, silver tone, 18k plated or 14k gold plated keeps a listing outside the Act. Where ASOS does claim precious metal it says so directly: a search for sterling silver returned 240 styles from £4.00 to £255.00.

faqs.q: Should a cheap silver item from ASOS carry a hallmark?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. Hallmarking is only required above 1g for gold, 7.78g for silver, 0.5g for platinum and 1g for palladium. A £6.00 pair of 10mm sterling silver hoops will fall below 7.78g, so it can lawfully be sold as silver with no mark. A heavier piece such as a £100 925 silver bracelet should carry three compulsory marks: the sponsor's mark, the assay office mark and the fineness mark.

faqs.q: Who do I complain to about a vintage item bought on ASOS?
faqs.a: The boutique named on the listing, in the first instance. ASOS's terms state that where an item is sold and shipped by a Brand Partner you contract with that partner, with ASOS Payments UK Limited (13337408) handling only the payment; where a partner's item is shipped by ASOS, ASOS.com Limited (3584121) is the seller. Brand Partner returns are free and go direct to the brand, taking up to 10 calendar days to be received and processed and up to 15 for some brands.

faqs.q: Is a vintage gold piece without a hallmark legitimate?
faqs.a: It can be. An article manufactured before 1950 may be described and sold as precious metal with no hallmark, provided the seller can prove it is of minimum fineness — 375 parts per thousand for gold, 800 for silver — and has had no improper alteration since 1950. Platinum made before 1 January 1975 and palladium before 1 January 2010 are also exempt. The proof is the seller's responsibility, which on an ASOS vintage listing means the boutique's.

title: ATS Euromaster Servicing: What You Can Still Claim, and Where the Work Goes
meta_title: ATS Euromaster Servicing: Your Guarantee Is Still Payable
meta_description: ATS Euromaster stopped servicing cars on 1 May 2026, yet five non-tyre guarantee categories are still paid. The claim route and the evidence needed.

headline.label: Full service, cheapest advertised price
headline.value: No longer sold — servicing and MOT work stopped at all 152 UK centres on 1 May 2026

intro:
ATS Euromaster is still settling guarantee claims on work it did before it shut, and its claim form, checked on 1 October 2026, shows that five of its six categories are service and repair work rather than tyres: brakes, brake parts, oil, air and fuel filters and spark plugs; steering and suspension shocks and coils; exhausts and catalytic converters; batteries; and TPMS sensors. That is a service invoice, item by item, and the form is still live on the company's own site.

The centres themselves have gone. Servicing and MOT testing ended at all 152 UK points of sale on 1 May 2026, and ATS Euromaster Limited is winding its UK business down. Forty-nine sites reopened under other names — 35 with Formula One Autocentres and 14 with S&M Tyres Limited, trading as Elite Garages — so a good number of former ATS workshops are still turning work round, with different signs over the door and different price lists inside.

The company behind the guarantee is in better shape than a closure usually leaves one. ATS Euromaster Limited, number 04303731, was still listed as Active at Companies House on 1 October 2026, with full accounts to 31 December 2025 filed on 25 July 2026 and no strike-off, administration or liquidation filing anywhere on the record. There is a solvent company to claim against, a published form to claim on, and a statutory remedy underneath it. This page sets out what a service customer can still recover, what the evidence has to look like, and what the next garage ought to be charging.
