sections.heading: Five of the six guarantee categories are service work
sections.html:
The ATS Warranties Claim Form is the only guarantee document the company still publishes, and it is a servicing document far more than a tyre one. Masterservice, the tyre scheme, is a single line on it. The other five cover brakes, brake parts, oil, air and fuel filters and spark plugs; steering and suspension, specifically shocks and coils; exhausts and catalytic converters; batteries; and TPMS sensors — between them, most of what comes off a routine interim or full service and most of what a fast-fit chain sells as a repair.

Each category sets its own evidence bar. A brake or exhaust claim needs an image of the old item clearly showing the defect or damage to the part being replaced, the original invoice, the new invoice and the new job sheet. Steering, suspension and TPMS claims need the three documents without the photograph. A battery claim needs a battery health report alongside them. Only the tyre line carries a settlement scale — free replacement at 6mm of remaining tread or more, 65% off between 4mm and 6mm, 35% between 2mm and 4mm, nothing below 2mm — and a service claim has no equivalent published ladder at all.

What a claimant is told in writing is short and worth having: the company says it is committed to honouring any valid warranty it previously provided on its goods and services, Masterservice included. Claims go to gen.uk.warranty@euromaster.com on the form. Complaints about goods or services already supplied go somewhere different — feedback@euromaster.com — and for a disputed service rather than a failed part, that second address is the one that matters.

sections.heading: The form sets no clock, which cuts both ways
sections.html:
Read the form looking for a duration and there is nothing there. Not twelve months, not 12,000 miles, not two years — no period and no mileage limit appears against any of the six categories. Compare that with a trading chain: Kwik Fit guarantees service components and other mechanical parts for 12 months or 12,000 miles, and National Tyres and Autocare publishes a minimum of two years or 24,000 miles. Against those, an unstated term is genuinely ambiguous rather than generous.

The terms that would have settled it are gone. The website is now a short closure notice and a link to the claim form, so nobody can read the duration, the exclusions or the conditions of the guarantee they are claiming under. A reader with a two-year-old service invoice has no way of knowing from any published ATS document whether the parts on it were ever covered for that long.

The practical reading is to claim and let the company say no in writing. There is no fee, the form is one document, and a refusal that quotes a term is itself evidence of what the term was. The alternative — waiting for clarity that no longer exists anywhere — runs down the statutory clock described below for nothing.

sections.heading: A service is not a product, and the remedies are different
sections.html:
This is the part most readers get wrong, because the consumer law everyone quotes is about goods. Fitting a part is a sale of goods; the labour, the diagnosis and the checks around it are a service, and Chapter 4 of the Consumer Rights Act 2015 governs them separately. Section 49 writes into every service contract a term that the trader must perform the service with reasonable care and skill. Section 52 adds performance within a reasonable time where none was agreed, and section 51 a reasonable price where none was fixed.

The remedy ladder is where a closed garage changes the answer. Section 55 gives the consumer the right to require the trader to perform the service again, within a reasonable time and without significant inconvenience, with the trader bearing all the cost — and it says that right is not available where completing performance in conformity with the contract is impossible. For a workshop that shut on 1 May 2026, it is impossible by definition. Section 56 then gives the right to a price reduction instead, and sets out how it has to be paid: refunded within 14 days, by the same means the consumer used to pay, with no fee for making the refund.

So a service complaint against ATS Euromaster is a money claim rather than a put-it-right claim, and it always will be. Two backstops sit behind it and each is worth a sentence: section 75 of the Consumer Credit Act 1974 makes a credit card provider jointly liable with the trader on purchases above £100, and a debit card payment can be taken back through chargeback under the card scheme rules. Both routes answer to someone who is still trading.

sections.heading: Your MOT record outlived the test station
sections.html:
Nothing in a vehicle's MOT history is lost when the garage that carried out the tests closes, because the record was never the garage's to keep. The free service at gov.uk holds car, motorcycle and van tests from 2005 onwards — 2018 for HGVs, trailers, buses and coaches, 2017 for Northern Ireland — and shows whether each test was passed or failed, the mileage recorded when it was tested, when the next one is due, which parts failed at each test and which had minor problems. Current and previous certificates can be downloaded, and any outstanding safety recall is flagged alongside.

Where each test was done is shown too, though that detail needs the 11-digit number from the V5C log book rather than just the registration. For anyone selling a car that was looked after at an ATS branch, that matters: the mileage trail and the advisory history are the part of a service record a buyer can verify independently, and they do not depend on a stamp from a company whose workshops have shut.

Whether ATS Euromaster could update a manufacturer's digital service record is a separate question, and one that can no longer be checked — the pages that would have said so are gone, so this page does not claim an answer either way. It is worth asking the next garage directly, because on most cars sold new in the last decade there is no paper book to stamp.

sections.heading: What the next garage should be charging for the test
sections.html:
The MOT fee is capped by the state, which makes it the one price in motoring a reader can check before they ring. The maxima are £54.85 for a car with up to eight passenger seats, £64 for a class 4 vehicle with nine to twelve passenger seats including a seat belt installation check, £58.60 for a petrol, diesel or hybrid goods vehicle over 3,000kg and up to 3,500kg, and £29.65 for a motorcycle, rising to £37.80 with a sidecar. These are ceilings and not prices, so a garage quoting under them is normal and a garage quoting over them is wrong.

The cap also exposes what a bundle really costs. Where a garage prices a service with the test included, subtracting the service-only price gives the figure it is charging for the MOT, and that number can be set against £54.85 directly. It is the cleanest comparison available on a servicing page and almost nobody does it out loud.

Two deadlines are worth knowing. A vehicle's first MOT falls due on the third anniversary of registration, and a test can be taken up to a month minus a day before the current certificate expires without losing the renewal date. Driving without a valid MOT carries a fine of up to £1,000, with an exception for driving to a pre-arranged test. Supply is not the problem — Great Britain had 23,092 private MOT test stations and 222 other stations in the 2025 to 2026 financial year, with 66,925 nominated testers, so the 152 ATS sites were under one per cent of the network.

The case for booking a service and a test together sits in DVSA's own quarterly figures. In the first quarter of 2026 to 2027, April to June, 26.75% of class 3 and 4 vehicles failed at the initial test. Lamps, reflectors and electrical equipment accounted for 9.98% of all tests, suspension 8.21%, tyres 6.55%, brakes 5.83% and visibility 4.40%. Bulbs, wipers, tyres and brake wear are service-sheet items, and they are where the failures come from.

sections.heading: The 49 sites that reopened, and what they charge now
sections.html:
Thirty-five former ATS centres went to Formula One Autocentres and fourteen to S&M Tyres Limited, trading as Elite Garages, with 216 staff transferring under TUPE across the 49 sites. Both buyers service cars and both took on branches with the ramps, the lifts and in many cases the same technicians already in them.

Elite Garages publishes its prices, which makes it the easier of the two to check: a standard service from £103 and a premium service from £180, with oil and filter, spark plugs where applicable, brake and clutch fluid checks, a handbrake operation and travel check, tread depths recorded and pressures reset. Its own note that additional service operations may be required for a particular make or model and will be charged at extra cost is fair warning that the figure is a floor. The branch list stood at 37 locations on 1 October 2026, across Kent, Sussex, Surrey, Hampshire, Dorset, Devon, Cornwall and the south west, a little under the 38 reported when the ATS sites were taken on in April 2026.

One caution for anyone choosing an independent over a franchised dealer. Having a car serviced outside the manufacturer's network does not cost the owner the manufacturer's warranty, and the rule that says so is British law rather than the European regulation garages still cite — the Competition Act 1998 (Motor Vehicle Agreements Block Exemption) Order 2023, SI 2023 No. 501, made on 28 April 2023, in force from 1 June 2023 and running to 31 May 2029. Elite Garages' own servicing page still explains the point by reference to European legislation. The answer it gives the customer is the right one; the authority it cites stopped being the operative one more than three years ago.

sections.heading: The dates on the public record worth watching
sections.html:
A claim against a closed company is only as good as the company's continued existence, so the register is the thing to keep an eye on. ATS Euromaster Limited's last filing was its full accounts to 31 December 2025, 46 pages, filed on 25 July 2026. Its confirmation statement is due on 26 October 2026 and its next accounts are due on 30 September 2027. It sits at SIC 45200, maintenance and repair of motor vehicles, with Michelin above it through Associated Tyre Specialists (Investment) Limited.

Those two dates are the signal. A company that files its confirmation statement on time is being maintained; a company that stops filing attracts a strike-off, and once it is dissolved its assets pass to the Crown as bona vacantia and a claimant is left applying to court to restore it. Anyone sitting on an ATS invoice has a reason to act before 26 October 2026 rather than after it, whatever the limitation period technically allows.

The parent has been slower to update than the register. Michelin's UK distribution page was still describing ATS Euromaster in the present tense on 1 October 2026 — a network created in 1965 extending over 260 centres across the country, which has “become one of the leaders in the vehicle servicing in the UK” with over 50 years of experience, SafeContractor and CHAS approval from 1991 and the RoSPA Gold Award for five consecutive years between 2014 and 2018. A servicing claim in the present tense, five months after the last service was carried out. The same page is useful despite that, because it names the Michelin routes that do still work: Blackcircles, online since 2002 with a network of over 2,000 independent fitting garages, and Tructyre, with 70 centres and more than 550 qualified technicians.

pros: Five of the six guarantee categories on the claim form are service and repair work — brakes and brake parts, oil, air and fuel filters, spark plugs, shocks and coils, exhausts and catalytic converters, batteries and TPMS sensors
The company says in writing that it will honour any valid warranty it previously provided on its goods and services, and the claim form is still published and downloadable

This is a solvent wind-down: ATS Euromaster Limited was still Active on the register on 1 October 2026, with full accounts to 31 December 2025 filed on 25 July 2026 and no insolvency filing on the record
Two separate routes are published — gen.uk.warranty@euromaster.com for a warranty claim on the form, feedback@euromaster.com for a complaint about work already carried out
Section 56 of the Consumer Rights Act 2015 requires a price reduction to be refunded within 14 days, by the same means the customer paid, with no fee charged for the refund
The MOT history at gov.uk survives the closure intact — pass and fail results from 2005, recorded mileage, failed and minor items, and downloadable certificates
49 former branches are still open under Formula One Autocentres and Elite Garages, with 216 staff transferred, and Elite publishes servicing prices from £103 and £180
cons: No servicing, repair or MOT work has been sold since 1 May 2026, when all 152 UK points of sale stopped trading

The claim form states no guarantee period and no mileage limit against any of the six categories, and the terms that would have set one are no longer published anywhere — against Kwik Fit's 12 months or 12,000 miles and National's 2 years or 24,000 miles, that is a gap rather than a benefit
Only the tyre line has a published settlement scale; a brake, exhaust, battery, suspension or TPMS claim has no stated basis of settlement at all
Brake and exhaust claims need a photograph of the old part clearly showing the defect, which is impossible if the part was left with the garage that replaced it
Every claim needs the original invoice and job sheet, and no branch can reprint either — an incomplete form, or one without the stated supporting documents, will not be processed
Because repeat performance is impossible for a closed workshop under section 55 of the Consumer Rights Act 2015, a service complaint can only ever end in money, never in the work being put right

No alternative dispute resolution body is named on the closure notice, and accreditation to the Motor Ombudsman's Service and Repair Code could not be confirmed from the Ombudsman's own material — so there is no independent route above the company's own inbox
Neither buyer of the former branches has published any undertaking to honour an ATS Euromaster guarantee
Michelin's own UK distribution page still called ATS Euromaster one of the leaders in UK vehicle servicing, in the present tense, five months after the last service was carried out
verdict: As a place to get a car serviced, ATS Euromaster no longer exists, and nothing about the way it closed changes that. As a guarantee, it is still worth something: five of the six categories on its claim form are service and repair work, the form is published, the inbox is answered, and the company behind it was Active on the register on 1 October 2026 rather than in an administrator's hands. Anyone holding an ATS invoice for brakes, a battery, an exhaust, suspension work or a service should find it now, photograph the paperwork, and send a claim in while there is a company to send it to — the confirmation statement due on 26 October 2026 is the date to beat, because a strike-off ends the matter long before any limitation period does. Anyone who simply needs a service booking is better served by checking whether their old branch is one of the 49 that reopened, then measuring whatever it quotes for an MOT against the £54.85 the state allows.

faqs.q: Can I still claim on an ATS Euromaster service or repair guarantee?
faqs.a: Yes. The ATS Warranties Claim Form covers six categories, five of which are service and repair work: brakes and brake parts, oil, air and fuel filters and spark plugs; steering and suspension shocks and coils; exhausts and catalytic converters; batteries; and TPMS sensors. Complete it, attach the original invoice, the new invoice and the new job sheet — plus a photograph of the old part for a brake or exhaust claim, or a battery health report for a battery — and email it to gen.uk.warranty@euromaster.com. An incomplete form will not be processed.

faqs.q: How long is an ATS Euromaster service guarantee meant to last?
faqs.a: The claim form names no period and no mileage against any category, and the full terms are no longer published, so there is no way to answer this from the company's own documents. A trading comparison gives the shape of the market: Kwik Fit guarantees service components for 12 months or 12,000 miles and National Tyres and Autocare for a minimum of two years or 24,000 miles. The practical approach is to submit the claim and ask the company to quote the term if it refuses.

faqs.q: Is ATS Euromaster in liquidation?
faqs.a: No. On 1 October 2026 ATS Euromaster Limited, number 04303731, was listed as Active at Companies House, with full accounts to 31 December 2025 filed on 25 July 2026 and no strike-off, administration or liquidation filing on the record. Its confirmation statement is due on 26 October 2026 and its next accounts on 30 September 2027. It is a solvent wind-down, which is why there is still a company to claim against.

faqs.q: Will my MOT history disappear now the garage has closed?
faqs.a: No. MOT records belong to the DVSA, not the test station. The free check at gov.uk holds car, van and motorcycle tests from 2005, showing pass or fail, the mileage recorded at each test, the parts that failed, any minor problems, when the next test is due, and downloadable current and previous certificates. Where each test was carried out is also shown, using the 11-digit number from the V5C log book.

faqs.q: What should I pay for an MOT at a new garage?
faqs.a: Less than the statutory maximum, which is £54.85 for a car with up to eight passenger seats, £64 for a class 4 vehicle with nine to twelve seats including a seat belt installation check, £58.60 for a goods vehicle over 3,000kg and up to 3,500kg, and £29.65 for a motorcycle. Where a garage sells a service with the test included, subtract its service-only price to see what it is charging for the test, then compare that with £54.85.

faqs.q: Which garages took over the ATS Euromaster workshops?
faqs.a: Thirty-five sites went to Formula One Autocentres and fourteen to S&M Tyres Limited, trading as Elite Garages, with 216 staff transferring across the 49 branches. Elite listed 37 locations on 1 October 2026 across Kent, Sussex, Surrey, Hampshire, Dorset, Devon, Cornwall and the south west, with servicing from £103 and £180. Neither buyer has published any commitment to honour a guarantee issued by ATS Euromaster.

faqs.q: Does an independent service affect my manufacturer warranty?
faqs.a: No, provided the work is done to the maker's schedule with parts of the right quality. The rule in force in Great Britain is the Competition Act 1998 (Motor Vehicle Agreements Block Exemption) Order 2023, SI 2023 No. 501, made on 28 April 2023, in force from 1 June 2023 and running to 31 May 2029. A number of garage websites, Elite Garages' servicing page among them, still explain the point by reference to European legislation; the outcome for the customer is the same, but the authority has moved.

title: ATS Euromaster Tyres: The Chain Has Closed, the Guarantee Has Not
meta_title: ATS Euromaster Closed: Your Tyre Guarantee Still Stands
meta_description: ATS Euromaster stopped trading on 1 May 2026, but Masterservice tyre guarantees are still being paid. The claim route, the tread bands and where to go now.

headline.label: Cheapest 205/55 R16 tyre, fitted
headline.value: No longer sold — all 152 UK points of sale stopped trading on 1 May 2026

intro:
ATS Euromaster fitted tyres in Britain for 60 years, and it is still paying out on the guarantees it sold. A Masterservice tyre with 6mm or more of tread left when it is damaged is replaced free of charge; between 4mm and 6mm the claimant gets 65% off the replacement, and between 2mm and 4mm, 35%. Those bands come off the company's own claim form, checked on 22 September 2026.

The shops themselves have gone. ATS Euromaster Limited began a structured wind-down of its UK business on 18 February 2026 and its last trading day was 1 May 2026, closing 152 points of sale. Thirty-five of them were sold to Formula One Autocentres and fourteen to Elite Garages, so 49 sites are still open under new signs; the other 103, the head office and the call centre closed for good, with 703 roles at risk.

What that leaves a motorist with is a piece of paper and an email address. Claims go to a single warranty inbox, the company is still listed as active at Companies House rather than in liquidation, and there is a six-year clock on the whole thing. This page sets out what is still claimable, what the evidence has to look like, and which garage now stands where your branch used to.

key_facts.value: ATS Euromaster Limited, registered number 04303731, Birmingham — still active on the register

sections.heading: The guarantee survived the shops
sections.html:
The single most useful sentence left on the ATS Euromaster website is this one: “We are committed to honouring any valid warranty ATS Euromaster has previously provided on its goods and services, including Masterservice.” That is unusual. A closing retailer normally leaves customers to argue with an administrator, and there is no administrator here.

The mechanism is a two-page document, the ATS Warranties Claim Form, still downloadable from the company's own domain. It covers seven categories of work: steering and suspension, meaning shocks and coils; brakes and brake parts; oil, air and fuel filters and spark plugs; Masterservice, which is the tyre guarantee; exhausts and catalytic converters; batteries; and TPMS sensors. Completed forms go by email to gen.uk.warranty@euromaster.com.

Masterservice is settled on remaining tread depth rather than age, and the form prints the ladder. At 6mm or more the claimant gets a “replacement tyre FREE of charge”. Above 4mm and below 6mm it is a “65% discount on the price of the replacement tyre on the day”. Above 2mm and below 4mm it is 35%. Below 2mm there is no discount at all.

Read that last line against the law and it stings a little. The legal minimum tread across the central three-quarters of a car tyre is 1.6mm, so the cover stops with roughly 0.4mm of lawful life still on the tyre — the stretch when a driver is most likely to be nursing a damaged one to the end of the month.

sections.heading: What a claim has to have in it
sections.html:
The evidence requirements are specific and the form is blunt about what happens if they are missed: “Any incomplete form, or forms without the stated supporting documents will not be processed.”

For a Masterservice tyre claim, two receipts are needed — the original ATS Euromaster receipt for the tyre being claimed on, and the receipt for the replacement. For batteries, exhausts, brakes, steering and suspension and TPMS sensors, three documents are wanted instead: the original purchase invoice, the replacement invoice, and a job sheet setting out the defect. Exhaust and brake claims need a photograph as well, described as an “image of old item clearly showing defect or damage”.

The practical problem is obvious once the branches have gone. A receipt from a shop that closed on 1 May 2026 cannot be reprinted at the counter, and the job sheet a claim needs was usually handed over on the day and filed in a glovebox. Anyone who bought tyres or brakes at ATS in the past few years and still has the paperwork should photograph it now rather than hunt for it when a tyre splits.

Complaints about goods or services already supplied go to a different address, feedback@euromaster.com, and property enquiries to uk.questions@euromaster.com. No response time is published for any of the three.

sections.heading: Sixty years, two rounds of cuts, one last day
sections.html:
Michelin built the Associated Tyre Specialists network in Britain in the late 1960s — Michelin's own UK page dates the business to 1965, the group's corporate history to the end of that decade — and the Euromaster brand was created in 1991. At its height in the 1990s the chain ran roughly 525 centres. Ownership never moved far: ATS Euromaster Limited's controlling shareholder is Associated Tyre Specialists (Investment) Limited, company 02535892, and that company's own controller is Compagnie Générale des Établissements Michelin of France, both notified on 6 April 2016.

The retreat came in two steps. On 14 March 2025 the company confirmed it would close 86 service centres, about a third of the network, with up to 400 jobs at risk and more than 235 branches left. The plan then was to swap bricks for wheels: 125 mobile technicians and a franchise model of the kind Euromaster runs elsewhere in Europe. Trade coverage of the filed accounts at that point put losses at £20.6m for 2022 and £13.9m for 2023.

Eleven months later the rest went. Announcing the wind-down on 18 February 2026, group managing director Nick Harley said that “despite the team's massive efforts to reshape the business, improve financial performance, and secure a sustainable future, a combination of intense market competition, sluggish activity within the sector and rising costs have left us with no viable path forward to a break-even position”. Consultation ran to 30 April 2026, the TUPE transfers were set for 18 April, and every remaining site traded to 1 May.

sections.heading: Which garage stands where your branch was
sections.html:
Forty-nine of the 152 sites kept their doors open under different ownership, and in both cases the staff moved with the building.

Formula One Autocentres took 35, saving more than 130 jobs and taking its own network to 170 centres, with a stated target of 250. The sites it bought strengthened its coverage in the North East, North West, South West and Wales.

Elite Garages, trading as S&M Tyres, took 14 and began trading from them on Monday 20 April 2026, with 61 employees transferring. That took the family firm from 24 vehicle repair centres to 38. The branches are at Ashford, Aylesbury, Bridport, Cirencester, Coulsdon, Hanworth, Helston, Kingsbridge, Launceston, Leatherhead, Okehampton, Stroud, Tavistock and Winchester.

A third piece went to a sister company rather than a buyer: 13 mobile night technicians were offered transfer to Tructyre, Michelin's commercial tyre arm, which joined the group in 2018 and runs 70 centres with more than 550 technicians.

None of that, though, carries a guarantee with it. Neither Formula One Autocentres nor Elite Garages has published any undertaking to honour an ATS Euromaster warranty on a tyre they did not sell, and the ATS claim form routes every claim back to the Euromaster inbox rather than to a shop. Walking into the same building with the same receipt is not, on the published evidence, a route to a free tyre.

sections.heading: What is still enforceable, and for how long
sections.html:
A guarantee is a promise on top of the law, not instead of it. Section 23 of the Consumer Rights Act 2015 gives a buyer of faulty goods the right to repair or replacement, and puts the cost on the trader: it must be done “within a reasonable time and without significant inconvenience to the consumer”, and the trader must “bear any necessary costs incurred in doing so (including in particular the cost of any labour, materials or postage)”. That right is against the seller, which is the point that matters here — the seller still exists.

The clock is section 5 of the Limitation Act 1980: “an action founded on simple contract shall not be brought after the expiration of six years from the date on which the cause of action accrued.” In Scotland the equivalent period is five years. Six years from a 2026 purchase runs to 2032, which is longer than the tyre.

The risk is not insolvency but dissolution. Companies House still showed ATS Euromaster Limited as active on 22 September 2026, with full accounts to 31 December 2025 filed on 25 July 2026 and the next confirmation statement due by 26 October 2026, and no insolvency notice for the company appears in The Gazette. A solvent wind-down of this kind usually ends with the company being struck off. When that happens, section 1012 of the Companies Act 2006 bites: everything “vested in or held on trust for the company immediately before its dissolution… are deemed to be bona vacantia and accordingly belong to the Crown”. There is a remedy — section 1029 lets “any person appearing to the court to have an interest in the matter” apply to restore a dissolved company — but a court application over one tyre is not a realistic answer.

Two cheaper backstops exist for anyone who paid by card. Section 75 of the Consumer Credit Act 1974 makes a credit card provider jointly liable with the retailer on purchases from £100 to £30,000, which covers most sets of four. Below that, a debit or credit card chargeback through the card scheme is the route, and it is the one worth using first, because it does not depend on the company answering an email.

The gap in all of this is dispute resolution. The ATS Euromaster website names no alternative dispute resolution scheme and no ombudsman, and whether the chain was ever accredited to the Motor Ombudsman's Service and Repair Code could not be confirmed from the Ombudsman's own material. A customer whose warranty claim is refused has the small claims track and nothing else published.

sections.heading: Michelin's own map still shows a chain that has gone
sections.html:
Michelin's UK site describes “an extensive distribution network in the UK with three entities: ATS Euromaster, a tyre and vehicle services provider, Blackcircles, an online tyre retailer and Tructyre, tyre fleet management experts”. The ATS entry, read on 22 September 2026, was still in the present tense and still credited the chain with “approximately 260 centres nationwide”, plus a run of ROSPA Gold awards from 2014 to 2018. The chain has not had 260 centres since early 2025 and has had none since 1 May 2026.

Nobody is being deceived out of money by a stale corporate page, but a driver who follows a manufacturer's own link expecting a fitting centre will find a notice instead. The two Michelin routes that do still work are on the same page: Blackcircles, online since 2002 and fitting through more than 2,000 independent garages, and Tructyre for commercial vehicles. The parent group itself is not shrinking — Euromaster reached 2,661 centres across Europe in 2026. Britain is simply no longer one of the places it runs them.

sections.heading: Where the record stops
sections.html:
Three things on this page are the best available rather than the last word, and they are worth naming.

The 2025 statutory accounts, 46 pages filed on 25 July 2026, would not open — the Companies House document service refused the request — so the final year's turnover, loss and closure provisions are not quoted here. The £20.6m and £13.9m losses above come from trade reporting of the earlier filings, not from the documents themselves.

Whether the 125 mobile technicians and the franchise model announced in March 2025 ever launched could not be established from any company source, and the mobile business does not appear in the February 2026 wind-down statement except as the 13 night technicians offered to Tructyre.

And the guarantee itself is now claimable but unreadable: the terms a Masterservice customer is claiming under — duration, exclusions, what counts as a valid claim — were on pages that have been replaced by the closure notice. The pro-rata ladder on the claim form is all that remains in public.

pros: Warranty claims are still being accepted and the company says in writing that it will honour any valid ATS Euromaster warranty, including Masterservice
The Masterservice settlement ladder is published in full — free replacement at 6mm or more, 65% off between 4mm and 6mm, 35% between 2mm and 4mm
This is a solvent wind-down, not an insolvency: the company was still active on the register on 22 September 2026, so there is a legal person to claim against
49 of the 152 sites kept trading with the same staff, 35 under Formula One Autocentres and 14 under Elite Garages
Michelin still reaches UK drivers through Blackcircles, with more than 2,000 independent fitting garages, and Tructyre's 70 commercial centres
cons: No tyres, servicing or MOTs are sold any more — every one of the 152 UK points of sale stopped trading on 1 May 2026
The warranty terms themselves are gone: the website is now a single closure notice, so a claimant cannot read the duration, exclusions or conditions of the guarantee being claimed under
Claims are email-only to one inbox, with no published response time, no named alternative dispute resolution scheme and no ombudsman route
“Any incomplete form, or forms without the stated supporting documents will not be processed” — and the receipts and job sheets required can no longer be reprinted by a branch
Masterservice pays nothing below 2mm of tread, while the legal minimum is 1.6mm, so the last stretch of a tyre's lawful life carries no cover at all
Neither buyer of the former branches has published any commitment to honour an ATS Euromaster guarantee
Michelin's own UK distribution page still advertised the chain in the present tense with “approximately 260 centres nationwide” more than four months after it closed
verdict: ATS Euromaster is no longer somewhere to buy a tyre, and no amount of good behaviour in the wind-down changes that. What it is, unusually, is a closed retailer still answering for its guarantees: the Masterservice ladder is published, the claim route works, and the company remains on the register rather than in the hands of an administrator. Anyone holding an ATS receipt should dig it out, photograph it, and send a claim in while there is still a company to send it to — the six-year limitation period is generous, but a strike-off would end the matter long before it expires. Anyone simply looking for four tyres should go to whoever now occupies the building, or to one of Michelin's remaining UK routes.

faqs.q: Is ATS Euromaster still open?
faqs.a: No. ATS Euromaster Limited announced a structured wind-down of its UK operations on 18 February 2026 and its final trading day was 1 May 2026. All 152 points of sale closed, although 49 of the buildings reopened under Formula One Autocentres or Elite Garages.

faqs.q: Can I still claim on an ATS Euromaster tyre guarantee?
faqs.a: Yes. The company says it will honour any valid warranty it previously provided, including Masterservice. Download the ATS Warranties Claim Form from its website, attach the original ATS receipt and the receipt for the replacement tyre, and email it to gen.uk.warranty@euromaster.com. Settlement depends on remaining tread: free at 6mm or above, 65% off between 4mm and 6mm, 35% between 2mm and 4mm, and nothing below 2mm.

faqs.q: Did ATS Euromaster go bust?
faqs.a: It did not enter administration or liquidation. The business was wound down by its owner after sustained losses, and the company was still listed as active at Companies House on 22 September 2026, with accounts for the year to 31 December 2025 filed on 25 July 2026 and no insolvency notice in The Gazette. That distinction matters for anyone with a claim: there is still a company to claim against.

faqs.q: How long do I have to bring a claim?
faqs.a: Section 5 of the Limitation Act 1980 gives six years from the date the cause of action arose for a claim founded on simple contract, and five years in Scotland. The practical limit is shorter: once a company is dissolved its assets become bona vacantia under section 1012 of the Companies Act 2006, and recovering anything then means a court application to restore it.

faqs.q: Who took over my local ATS branch?
faqs.a: Formula One Autocentres bought 35 sites, taking its network to 170 centres. Elite Garages bought 14 — Ashford, Aylesbury, Bridport, Cirencester, Coulsdon, Hanworth, Helston, Kingsbridge, Launceston, Leatherhead, Okehampton, Stroud, Tavistock and Winchester — and started trading from them on 20 April 2026. The remaining 103 sites closed.

faqs.q: Where can I buy Michelin tyres in the UK now?
faqs.a: Michelin's UK distribution now runs through Blackcircles, which has sold online since 2002 and fits through more than 2,000 independent garages, and Tructyre, its commercial arm, with 70 centres and more than 550 technicians. Michelin tyres are also stocked by every national fast-fit chain.

title: Audi New Cars Review 2026: Prices, Tax and Warranty Limits
meta_title: Audi New Cars 2026: Range Prices From £24,870
meta_description: What a new Audi costs in October 2026: range prices from £24,870 to £89,555, the £440 tax supplement, the 60,000-mile warranty cap and the EV charger offer.

headline.label: Cheapest new Audi, on the road
headline.value: £24,870 — A1 Sportback, the entry point to a 17-model range (franchised Audi retailer list, prices correct at 22 July 2026)

intro:
The cheapest new Audi on sale in the UK is an A1 Sportback at £24,870; the dearest listed is an e-tron GT at £89,555. Both figures were read on 2 October 2026 from a franchised Audi retailer's published range list, which states its prices were correct at 22 July 2026 — Audi's own UK site shows no price at all until you open the configurator. Between those two numbers sit 17 model lines and 62 derivatives, from a three-cylinder hatchback to a 250kW electric SUV.

Order any electric or plug-in hybrid Audi between 1 October 2026 and 5 January 2027 and the published terms give you a 7kW Ohme home charger with standard installation, or £500 instead. Every new Audi carries three years of warranty, a 12-year anti-perforation guarantee, and — on the fully electric cars — eight years or 100,000 miles of battery degradation cover.

The finance is not Audi's. Audi Financial Services is a trading name of Volkswagen Financial Services (UK) Limited, authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority under firm reference 311988, and that matters more in 2026 than it has in any year since the brand arrived here.

sections.heading: The price ladder, and the fact that Audi will not print it
sections.html:
Audi UK's model pages name every car and price none of them. The models index lists A1, A2 e-tron, A3, A5, A6, A6 e-tron, A8, Q2, Q3, Q4 e-tron, Q5, Q6 e-tron, Q7, Q8, Q9, e-tron GT and Nuvolari — 17 lines and 62 individual derivatives — under a single line of small print saying prices relate to the UK base-specification model and exclude optional equipment. The number itself is behind the configurator, and so is the finance quote.

The prices below come from a franchised Audi retailer's published range list, read on 2 October 2026, which states the figures were correct at 22 July 2026 and include VAT at the prevailing rate:

  • A1 from £24,870
  • Q2 from £30,660
  • A3 from £30,895
  • Q3 from £39,065
  • A5 from £43,510
  • Q4 e-tron from £46,955
  • Q5 from £53,110
  • A6 from £54,835
  • Q6 e-tron from £61,315
  • A6 e-tron from £63,365
  • Q7 from £73,225
  • Q8 from £82,120
  • A8 from £85,840
  • e-tron GT from £89,555

A second franchised retailer's live stock list on the same day priced a physical car rather than a range: an A1 Sportback 30 TFSI Sport at £25,029. The two figures are £159 apart, which is the useful part — the entry price to the brand is a shade under £25,000 and has been all summer. Treat any single quoted number as a starting point for one specification on one day, because the only place a binding price exists is an Audi Centre's order form.

sections.heading: What the list price costs you at the DVLA
sections.html:
Vehicle tax on a new car is charged twice over, and the second charge is the one buyers miss. The first-year rate is set by carbon dioxide output. For a car first registered on or after 1 April 2017 the bands run from £10 at zero emissions, through £115 at 1–50g/km, £135 at 51–75g/km, £280 at 76–90g/km, £365 at 91–100g/km, £405 at 101–110g/km, £455 at 111–130g/km and £560 at 131–150g/km, to £5,690 above 255g/km. A diesel that does not meet the RDE2 standard pays the next band up: £1,410 rather than £560 at 131–150g/km.

Audi's own model-year 2026 product guide puts the A3 35 TFSI S tronic at 126–129g/km, which lands it in the 111–130 band at £455 for the first year. The guide readable on 2 October 2026 was the Irish-market edition, so the UK configurator is worth checking for the exact derivative before you budget on it; the band boundary at 130g/km is £105 wide and some options push a car over it.

From the second year every car pays the standard £200 a year. On top of that, a car with a list price above £40,000 — or above £50,000 if it is electric — pays an extra £440 a year for five years, starting from the second time it is taxed. That is £2,200 of additional tax, and on the price ladder above it catches the A5, Q5, A6, Q7, Q8, A8, the A6 e-tron, the Q6 e-tron and the e-tron GT outright. The Q3 at £39,065 sits £935 below the line before a single option is added; metallic paint alone can carry it over. The Q4 e-tron at £46,955 escapes, because the electric threshold is £10,000 higher.

sections.heading: Buying an Audi means borrowing from Volkswagen
sections.html:
Audi's regulatory page names two firms. Volkswagen Financial Services (UK) Limited holds the FCA authorisation under firm reference 311988, from Brunswick Court, Yeomans Drive, Blakelands, Milton Keynes MK14 5LR. Volkswagen Insurance Service (Great Britain) Limited operates as its appointed representative. Audi Financial Services, the name on the agreement, is a trading style rather than a separate company, and the Audi Centre selling the car acts as credit broker.

The complaints route is published and short. A complaint is acknowledged within five working days; if it is not resolved within eight weeks a holding letter is issued, and at that point the customer can take it to the Financial Ombudsman Service. The Customer Resolutions Department is reachable on 0800 912 3564 or at customerresolutions@vwfs.co.uk.

The Ombudsman's own figures give the scale of motor finance disputes. Between April and June 2026 it received 53,600 new complaints across all products, of which 5,647 concerned motor hire purchase — upheld in 16% of decided cases — alongside 708 conditional sale complaints at a 20% uphold rate and 97 motor point-of-sale loans at 35%. The Ombudsman notes that unresolved commission cases depress the overall uphold rate, which stood at 26% across every product in the quarter.

sections.heading: The 2024 enforcement notice, and the redress machinery running now
sections.html:
On 21 October 2024 the FCA fined Volkswagen Financial Services (UK) Limited £5,397,600 over its treatment of customers in financial difficulty between 1 January 2017 and 31 July 2023. The penalty was discounted 30% for settlement from £7,710,885.73. The notice found breaches of Principles 3, 6 and 7, of CONC 7.2.1R, 7.3.4R, 7.3.9R and 7.3.14R(1), and of DISP 1.3.1R, and recorded 109,589 customers who suffered harm or were put at risk of it. By the date of the notice the firm had paid £17,823,500 to 80,191 customers, with total redress estimated at £21,506,496. Reading the notice, the recurring failure is templated arrears correspondence that obscured the help available rather than offering it.

Separately, the FCA's motor finance consumer redress scheme is being worked through across the industry, and Volkswagen Financial Services wrote a great many of the agreements inside it. The scheme is split in two: Scheme 1 covers agreements from 6 April 2007 to 31 March 2014 and Scheme 2 from 1 April 2014 to 1 November 2024. Where redress is due it is calculated as the average of an estimated loss figure and the commission actually paid, plus interest, with the loss element built on an APR adjustment of 21% for Scheme 1 and 17% for Scheme 2. Interest is simple, at the annual average Bank of England base rate plus 1%, with a floor of 3% in any year.

The deadline needs care. The policy statement sets an implementation period ending 30 June 2026 for agreements from April 2014 onwards and 31 August 2026 for earlier ones, with six further months to opt in — so 31 December 2026 and 28 February 2027 respectively. A separate FCA briefing published alongside it gives 31 August 2027 as a final date. The two documents do not read the same way and this needs confirming with the lender rather than assumed; if you financed an Audi before November 2024, ask Volkswagen Financial Services in writing which date applies to your agreement.

sections.heading: Electric Audis: the range Audi quotes and the grant it misses
sections.html:
Audi's own engineering figures are published, even where its prices are not. The press material issued from Ingolstadt on 27 April 2026 gives the updated Q4 e-tron two batteries — 63kWh gross and 59kWh net, or 82kWh gross and 77kWh net — and outputs of 150, 210, 220 and 250kW. WLTP range tops out at 440km for the SUV, 451km for the Sportback, and 592km for the Sportback e-tron performance, which is about 368 miles. Direct current charging runs at 160–165kW, rising to 185kW on the quattro performance, and 10% to 80% takes 27 minutes at a fast charger.

None of it qualifies for the Electric Car Grant. The grant pays £3,750 in its top band and £1,500 in the second, and is capped at a recommended retail price of £37,000 — a figure that includes VAT, the manufacturer's or dealer's mandatory extras, delivery and administration charges, and the cost of the battery even where the battery is leased. The cheapest electric Audi on the list above is the Q4 e-tron at £46,955, which is £9,955 clear of the ceiling. Manufacturers, not buyers, apply for eligibility through the Office for Zero Emission Vehicles and the Vehicle Certification Agency, and must either hold targets verified by the Science Based Targets initiative or score level 4 or higher in the Transition Pathway Initiative's auto sector assessment.

What Audi offers instead is the charger. The published terms for orders and deliveries between 1 October 2026 and 5 January 2027 cover the A6 e-tron, Q4 e-tron, Q6 e-tron and e-tron GT, plus the plug-in hybrid A3, A5, A6, A8, Q3, Q5, Q7 and Q8, and give the customer a 7kW Ohme Home Pro with a 5m tethered cable, a 7kW untethered Ohme ePod, or £500 including VAT. Installation is by Ohme Operations UK Ltd, within a month before delivery or up to three months after, and the customer must be a homeowner or a renter with the landlord's permission, with off-street parking. One incentive per customer, nothing retrospective, and Fleet Sales Direct orders are excluded.

There is a reason the electric cars are the ones carrying an incentive. Under the Vehicle Emissions Trading Schemes, as set out in the government's June 2026 compliance guidance, 33% of a manufacturer's new cars must be zero emission in 2026, rising to 38% in 2027, and a missed allowance costs £12,000. Manufacturers may borrow against future years to 2029 at 3.5% compounding interest, capped in 2026 at 8.25% of total registrations, or convert carbon credits at 167:1. For context, SMMT's 2026 facts book records 2,020,520 new cars registered in 2025 with battery electric vehicles at 19.2% and average new car emissions of 91.8g/km, down 10.1% in the year. A brand selling £60,000 electric SUVs into a market that bought fewer than one in five electric is paying for the gap somewhere, and the home charger is part of how.

sections.heading: Safety scores, servicing and the three-year cliff edge
sections.html:
The newest Audi tested by Euro NCAP is the Q6 e-tron, assessed in 2024 as a quattro five-door SUV and rated 5 stars: 91% for adult occupant protection, 92% for child occupant, 81% for vulnerable road users and 80% for safety assist. Frontal impact protection was good for every critical body area of driver and passenger, with full marks for dummy measurements. The weaknesses are specific and worth knowing: poor results on the stiff windscreen pillars and at the base of the screen in pedestrian and cyclist head tests, poor pelvis protection at the edges of the bonnet leading edge, and only partial credit for fatigue detection because the system infers drowsiness rather than watching the driver.

The warranty is three years or 60,000 miles, whichever comes first, alongside three years of paintwork cover and 12 years against perforation by corrosion. Fully electric models add a high-voltage battery degradation warranty of eight years or 100,000 miles. Cover transfers to a new owner if the car is sold inside the term, with the exception of the plug-in hybrid battery warranty, and four- or five-year extensions can be bought at the point of purchase. The condition attached is servicing to Audi's recommendations within the stated mileage and time limits.

Servicing itself runs on two regimes for petrol, diesel and hybrid cars — Smart or Standard — and a single regime for the electric ones, with the car's MMI screen or the myAudi app calling the next visit. Audi offers fixed-price menu servicing on cars over three years old, a Service Price Match against a competitor quote using Audi Genuine Parts, and service plans spread over interest-free instalments at 0%. Several items sit outside an oil or inspection service and come due on their own schedule: air filter, pollen filter, spark plugs, fuel filter, brake fluid and gearbox oil.

sections.heading: Who takes the money
sections.html:
Audi UK is not a company. The entity behind the franchise is Volkswagen Group United Kingdom Limited, company number 00514809, incorporated on 1 January 1953 and registered at Yeomans Drive, Blakelands, Milton Keynes MK14 5AN — the same business park as the finance arm. It has traded as V.A.G. (United Kingdom) Limited and Volkswagen (G.B.) Limited. The dealer you sign with is a separate franchised business, and the credit agreement is with Volkswagen Financial Services (UK) Limited. Three companies, one logo.

Scale is easier to find at segment level than by brand. SMMT's 2026 facts book records 25,501 A3 registrations in 2025, 5.5% of the lower medium segment — a single Audi model outselling most manufacturers' entire UK ranges. That is the practical case for the brand: the residual values that make a four-year personal contract plan affordable are built on volumes like that, and they are the reason a £55,000 A6 can be advertised at a monthly figure a £35,000 rival cannot match.

pros: 17 model lines and 62 derivatives, from £24,870 to £89,555
12-year anti-perforation warranty, well beyond the three-year mechanical cover
Eight years or 100,000 miles of battery degradation cover on fully electric models
A 7kW Ohme home charger with standard installation, or £500, on electric and plug-in hybrid orders placed between 1 October 2026 and 5 January 2027
Q6 e-tron rated five stars by Euro NCAP in 2024, with 92% for child occupant protection
Q4 e-tron Sportback e-tron performance quoted at 592km WLTP, with 10–80% charging in 27 minutes at up to 185kW
Fixed-price menu servicing after three years, a Service Price Match and service plans at 0%
Complaints acknowledged in five working days, a final answer inside eight weeks, then a free route to the Financial Ombudsman Service
cons: Audi publishes no price on any readable page of its UK site. Every figure on this page had to come from franchised retailers' own lists — one of them dated 22 July 2026 — because the models, offers and electric pages all return nothing, and the pricelists on Audi's UK press site are years out of date.
The warranty is capped at 60,000 miles. A driver covering 20,000 miles a year is out of mechanical cover during year three, which is exactly the sort of mileage a diesel A6 is bought for.

Nine of the fourteen ranges listed are priced above the £40,000 tax threshold, so the £440 annual supplement applies for five years — £2,200 of tax that is invisible at the point of sale. The Q3 sits £935 below the line before options.
No electric Audi comes close to the £37,000 Electric Car Grant cap. The cheapest is £9,955 over it, so buyers get a home charger worth up to £999 instead of up to £3,750 off the price.

The finance arm was fined £5,397,600 by the FCA in October 2024 over its handling of 109,589 customers in financial difficulty between January 2017 and July 2023, and has paid £21,506,496 in related redress. Anyone taking an Audi on finance is borrowing from that firm.

Euro NCAP marked the Q6 e-tron down to 81% for vulnerable road users, citing poor results on the stiff windscreen pillars, and gave only partial credit for a fatigue system that infers drowsiness rather than monitoring the driver directly.
No service price is published anywhere on the site — fixed-price servicing, service plans and the Service Price Match are all described without a single figure attached.
The new car warranty page states no roadside assistance period at all; cover is described only for Approved Used cars.
verdict: Audi sells a wide, well-engineered range in the UK and backs it with 12 years against corrosion and eight years on an electric car's battery, which is more than the headline three-year warranty suggests. The entry price is a little under £25,000 for an A1 and climbs to £89,555 for an e-tron GT, and a buyer going electric before 5 January 2027 gets a 7kW home charger fitted or £500. The two things to settle before signing are both financial rather than mechanical. Nine of the fourteen ranges cross the £40,000 tax line, adding £440 a year for five years that nobody mentions in a showroom; and the credit agreement is with Volkswagen Financial Services (UK) Limited, FRN 311988, a firm fined £5,397,600 in 2024 for its treatment of customers who fell behind. Neither is a reason to avoid the cars. Both are reasons to read the agreement, ask for the on-the-road price in writing with the first-year tax itemised, and, if you financed an Audi before November 2024, ask the lender which redress deadline applies to you.

faqs.q: How much is the cheapest new Audi?
faqs.a: £24,870 for an A1 Sportback, taken from a franchised Audi retailer's range list that states its prices were correct at 22 July 2026. A second retailer's live stock list on 2 October 2026 priced a specific A1 Sportback 30 TFSI Sport at £25,029. Audi's own site publishes no price until you build a car in the configurator, so treat either figure as a starting point rather than a quote.

faqs.q: What does an Audi warranty actually cover, and for how long?
faqs.a: Three years or 60,000 miles, whichever comes first, plus three years of paintwork cover and 12 years against perforation by corrosion. Fully electric models add eight years or 100,000 miles of high-voltage battery degradation cover. The warranty transfers if you sell the car within the term, except for the plug-in hybrid battery warranty, and extensions to four or five years can be bought when you order. Servicing to Audi's schedule is a condition.

faqs.q: Will I get the government's electric car grant on an Audi?
faqs.a: No. The grant is worth £3,750 in its top band and £1,500 in the second, and is capped at a recommended retail price of £37,000 including VAT, delivery, admin charges and the battery. The cheapest electric Audi listed is the Q4 e-tron at £46,955, £9,955 above the cap. Audi's own incentive for electric and plug-in hybrid orders placed between 1 October 2026 and 5 January 2027 is a 7kW Ohme charger with standard installation, or £500.

faqs.q: How much tax will I pay on a new Audi?
faqs.a: A first-year rate set by emissions — £10 at zero, £455 in the 111–130g/km band, £560 at 131–150g/km and up to £5,690 above 255g/km — then £200 a year as standard. If the list price is over £40,000, or over £50,000 for an electric car, add £440 a year for five years from the second time the car is taxed. That supplement catches the A5, Q5, A6, Q7, Q8, A8, A6 e-tron, Q6 e-tron and e-tron GT, and totals £2,200.

faqs.q: Who do I complain to about an Audi finance agreement?
faqs.a: Volkswagen Financial Services (UK) Limited, which trades as Audi Financial Services and is authorised by the FCA under firm reference 311988. Its Customer Resolutions Department is on 0800 912 3564 or customerresolutions@vwfs.co.uk, at Brunswick Court, Yeomans Drive, Blakelands, Milton Keynes MK14 5LR. A complaint is acknowledged within five working days and should get a final answer inside eight weeks; after that, or if you are unhappy with the outcome, the Financial Ombudsman Service will look at it free of charge.

faqs.q: Does the car finance redress scheme cover Audi agreements?
faqs.a: It covers agreements written between 6 April 2007 and 1 November 2024 where a discretionary or high commission arrangement applied, split into Scheme 1 to 31 March 2014 and Scheme 2 from 1 April 2014, and Volkswagen Financial Services wrote a large share of them. Redress is the average of an estimated loss and the commission paid, plus simple interest at the Bank of England base rate plus 1% with a 3% annual floor. The FCA's own documents state the opt-in deadline differently in two places, so ask your lender in writing which date applies to your agreement.

title: Autotrader Sell My Car
meta_title: Autotrader Sell My Car: Free Dealer Auction in 48 Hours
meta_description: Sell to 5,000+ trade buyers for £0, free collection, same-day payment in 48 hours. What the free route costs you, and the 49% joint venture behind it.

headline.label: What selling costs you
headline.value: £0 — free dealer auction, free home collection and same-day payment in as little as 48 hours (a private advert costs extra and the price table is unreadable)

intro:
Autotrader will get your car sold for £0. More than 5,000 trade buyers bid against each other for it, collection from your door is free, payment is made the same day, and the highest offer can land in as little as 48 hours. Those are Autotrader's own terms from its sell-to-a-dealer pages, read on 2 October 2026.

It is also the largest audience in the country to sell into. Autotrader's results for the year to 31 March 2026 report over nine million unique visitors a month spending 548 million minutes on the site, 11 times the time given to its nearest rival and six times that given to all its main competitors combined, against an average 451,000 cars advertised. The business has been doing this since John Madejski started a regional classified magazine called Thames Valley Trader in 1977; it put up its first website in 1996 and listed in London on 24 March 2015.

One thing is worth knowing before you start, and it is a point in the service's favour rather than against it. The free route is not Autotrader buying your car. It is run through Dealer Auction, the trade wholesale marketplace Autotrader owns 49% of, so your car goes into a live auction in front of professional buyers rather than to one firm quoting one price. The dealer who wins it is the paying customer; you are not.

sections.heading: Two ways out of a car, and they do not cost the same
sections.html:
Autotrader offers a private seller two entirely separate products, and the money runs in opposite directions.

The dealer auction is free. You enter the registration, add the detail and the photographs, and Dealer Auction's buyers bid. Autotrader's own page quotes over 5,000 trusted dealers, a sale in 48 hours or less, free collection from your home and same-day payment. The marketplace behind it is Dealer Auction Limited, company number 11514206, which advertises more than 4,000 registered sellers, over 5,000 active trade buyers, 11,000 fresh vehicles added a month and 600 auctions ending every day. That is a real wholesale market, not a single buying desk, and it is the reason the competition between bidders is worth something.

The private advert is not free, and this is where the page runs into a wall. Autotrader prices private adverts by how much the vehicle is worth — its help centre says you must "select whether you're a private or trade seller, and the correct price band for how much your vehicle is worth", that cars and vans are priced differently in Great Britain and Northern Ireland, and that "the package to keep your advert live until sold is only available for cars being sold privately". The price table itself sits at autotrader.co.uk/sell-my-car/advertising-prices and it does not render to anything a reader or a machine can read: the page returns "Hmm, seems there's no items to display" where the figures should be, and the same template is empty for vans, so the numbers load client-side. We could not verify a single private advert price and are not going to guess one — get it on screen before you commit, because the price band is decided by your car's value rather than by a flat fee.

What the advert buys is reach. Autotrader puts the private seller audience at over 9.5 million people each month, which it describes as 3.5 times its competitors.

sections.heading: £23.6m, falling 11%, and what that says about the paid advert
sections.html:
Autotrader is a listed company, so the sell-side of its business is audited rather than asserted. The figures below are from the full-year results published on 21 May 2026, covering the year to 31 March 2026.

  • Group revenue: £624.3m, up 4% from £601.1m
  • Operating profit: £392.7m, up 4% from £376.8m
  • Basic earnings per share: 34.17p, up 8% from 31.66p
  • Consumer Services revenue: £38.8m, down 8% from £42.4m
  • Private revenue — what people like you pay to advertise: £23.6m, down 11% from £26.6m
  • Share of profit from Dealer Auction: £4.1m, up 14% from £3.6m
  • Average retailer forecourts advertising: 13,942, down 0.5% from 14,013

Read those last three lines together and the shape of the business is clear. The money private sellers hand over is shrinking by double digits a year while the money made from the trade buying their cars is growing. Autotrader is not hiding this: the results state plainly that private revenue comes from "individual sellers who pay to advertise their vehicle on the Autotrader marketplace" and that the Dealer Auction profit rose on "a higher volume of vehicle transactions".

For a seller that is mostly good news, because it means the free route is the one the company has every reason to keep improving. The caution is the other half of the same fact: a product with revenue falling 11% a year is not usually the one getting the investment, and the unreadable price page is consistent with that.

sections.heading: What a used car is actually fetching the month you sell it
sections.html:
Autotrader publishes a monthly retail price index, and the August 2026 edition, released on 8 September 2026, is the number to argue from:

  • Average used car asking price: £17,131, down 0.1% year on year and 0.4% on the month
  • Average days to sell: 30
  • Transactions: up 2.6% year on year
  • Cars aged 10 to 15 years: £7,183, up 6.9% — the strongest band in the market
  • Cars aged one to three years: down 1.8%
  • Used electric cars: £25,095 average, up 3.8%, selling in 27 days; three-to-five-year-old electric models up 9.4% to £20,351

Two independent checks are worth running against that. The Office for National Statistics measures second-hand car prices inside the inflation figures, and its annual rate for August 2026, released on 16 September 2026, was -2.5%, having moved from +0.4% in March through -1.2% in June and -1.9% in July. The two series are not contradicting each other: one tracks what sellers are asking on a forecourt, the other what buyers actually pay across the whole second-hand market, and the gap is the discount being negotiated. On volume, the Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders counted 2,009,318 used car transactions in the second quarter of 2026, up 0.7%, for a first-half total of 4,025,550; battery electric transactions jumped 67.0% to 110,761 and took a record 5.5% share, while petrol slipped 1.2% to 1,121,243 and diesel fell 7.2% to 620,045.

If your car is a ten-year-old petrol hatchback, that market is running in your favour. If it is an eighteen-month-old lease return, it is not.

Autotrader's free valuation tool is a reasonable starting point for either. It is built on over 800,000 adverts and prices shared by over 3,500 dealer websites plus auction and ex-fleet data, and it is refreshed daily. Note what it assumes: a car "in good condition for its age" with minor wear and tear only, with service history gaps, damage and missing MOT certificates all capable of pulling the real figure below the estimate. It quotes a private sale price and a part-exchange price separately, which is the honest way to show it.

sections.heading: Whose company you are actually dealing with
sections.html:
The brand changed its spelling this year and the paperwork records it. Autotrader Limited, company number 03909628, was incorporated on 19 January 2000 and sits at No.3 Circle Square, 3 Hawkshaw Street, Manchester M1 7BL. Companies House shows it trading as AUTO TRADER LIMITED until 16 January 2026 and, before March 2014, as TRADER PUBLISHING LIMITED. Its registered activity code is still 58142 — publishing of consumer and business journals and periodicals — which is a small monument to a business that started as a magazine on a newsagent's shelf. The listed parent is Autotrader Group plc, company 09439967. The group employed 1,239 people at the end of March 2026, down from 1,290.

The limits of what the platform takes on are set out in its terms for online enquiries, deals and reservations, and they are blunter than most. "Autotrader is not a party to the sale of the Vehicle to you," it says, and "There will be a separate legal contract between you and the Dealer for the purchase of the Vehicle." Its liability under those terms "shall not in any circumstances exceed £0 in total". Where a buyer reserves a car through the site, the pre-authorised reservation payment is handled by Stripe and released within 7 days if the deal is not completed, and the terms are explicit that it "is not a Part payment or deposit towards the price of the Vehicle". That wording governs the buying journey rather than your sale, but it tells you how the company sees its role: it introduces, it does not underwrite.

On the buying side the same year brought real investment — Deal Builder reached 6,700 retailers from 2,000, with 175,000 vehicles live and 137,000 deals carrying a full reservation against 49,000 the year before. None of it changes what happens when something goes wrong with your sale: there is no financial regulator over the sale of a second-hand car and no ombudsman to escalate to, so your remedy is the dealer, the courts, or Autotrader's own complaints team.

sections.heading: The paperwork nobody else is going to do
sections.html:
Selling privately puts three jobs on you that a dealer sale would absorb.

Tell DVLA, and do it the day the car goes. Until the record changes you are the registered keeper, which means the speeding tickets and the parking charges are yours. GOV.UK is specific about the money: once you have told DVLA, "your vehicle tax will be cancelled" and you "get a refund for any full months of remaining vehicle tax" — full months only, so the timing of a sale is worth a few pounds. Tax does not travel with the car: "The tax is not transferred to you when you buy the vehicle", and your buyer has to tax it before driving away. Say so when you hand over the keys, because a buyer who drives off untaxed tends to ring the last keeper first.

Take the money carefully. UK Finance's Annual Fraud Report 2026 counted 175,809 purchase scam cases in 2025 costing £118.1m, an average of £671 a case, with losses up 20% on the year and cases up 5%. Across all authorised push payment fraud the figures were £576.4m and 248,070 cases, up 19% and 7%, with 78% of losses reimbursed to victims; 66% of cases began online, though those tend to be smaller and account for 32% of losses. Those numbers describe buyers being defrauded rather than sellers, which is exactly why a buyer standing on your drive will be nervous, and why a bank transfer that clears before the keys move is the normal answer.

Know what the rules stop other people doing. Since 6 April 2025, Schedule 20 of the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 lists practices banned in all circumstances. Paragraph 25 catches "falsely claiming or creating the false impression that the trader is not acting for purposes relating to the trader's business or falsely representing oneself as a consumer" — the trader hiding behind a private advert, which is the oldest trick in this market and now unlawful outright. Paragraph 13 does the same for fake and incentivised reviews. The point for you is that a genuine private seller is now competing against fewer disguised dealers, and that the same rule binds you if you are selling more than the odd car.

Autotrader's own advertising guidelines are stricter than you might expect and they apply to your listing. You must "state the full sale price of the vehicle" inclusive of everything on consumer channels, "state the full mileage" in full digits rather than abbreviated, and keep both consistent across the advert; prices shown as "£8000 + VAT" are removed or amended as misleading, as are adverts for a car that has already sold. The sting is in the enforcement line: "No refunds or credits will be given for adverts or videos removed for breaching guidelines."

sections.heading: Where this leaves a seller short
sections.html:
Four things deserve a seller's attention before they choose the free route.

Free means trade price, and Autotrader says so itself. Its part-exchange pages state that a part-exchange valuation "will be slightly less than what you would get if you sold your car privately" because "the dealer will be buying your car from you to resell it, meaning they'll incur costs for stocking and preparation". The same logic applies to the auction. The £17,131 average asking price in its own August index is a retail shop window, not a cheque to a private seller, and the 30 days a forecourt waits for that money is part of what the bidding dealer is pricing in.

The auction's small print is not on the auction page. The sell-to-a-dealer page sets out three steps, the 48-hour timescale, free collection and same-day payment, and stops. It does not say whether a winning offer can be reduced when the collecting dealer inspects the car, it publishes no list of vehicles the auction will not take — outstanding finance, category write-offs, imports, non-runners, high mileage — and it names no cancellation charge. Rivals in this category publish their refusals and their fees in a table. Read the terms the offer arrives with, and treat anything the headline page does not mention as unsettled rather than absent.

You cannot find out what an advert costs without starting one. A price list that will not display is a poor way to sell a paid product, and it makes the two routes impossible to compare on paper. Combined with private revenue falling 11% to £23.6m, it is hard to read the paid advert as a priority.

And the safety advice is odd. Autotrader's own guide to meeting a buyer says, in terms, "Always meet potential buyers at your home." The rest of that page is sound — ask for a driving licence, never let a stranger take the car out alone, check that your insurance or theirs covers the test drive, take a note of the car they arrive in, walk away if you feel uneasy — but handing your home address to everyone who answers an advert is a choice, not a default, and plenty of sellers will prefer a supermarket car park and a second person present. One more number from the same results, for context on a company in the middle of a lot of change: employee engagement fell 19 percentage points to 72%.

pros: The dealer auction costs the seller £0, with free home collection and same-day payment
Over 5,000 trade buyers bidding competitively, and a sale possible in 48 hours or less
Run through Dealer Auction Limited (company 11514206), a genuine wholesale market with 11,000 fresh vehicles a month and 600 auctions ending daily
The largest selling audience in the UK — over nine million unique visitors a month, 11x the nearest competitor
Free, no-obligation valuation built on 800,000+ adverts and 3,500+ dealer websites, refreshed daily, quoting private and part-exchange prices separately
Audited public-company figures rather than self-reported marketing numbers, published 21 May 2026
An "until sold" advert package exists and is reserved for private sellers
Advertising guidelines ban "+VAT" pricing, abbreviated mileage and adverts for cars already sold, which keeps honest listings competitive
cons: Private advert prices are set by vehicle value band and the price table does not display — we could not verify a single figure
The free route is a trade sale: Autotrader's own pages concede a dealer pays "slightly less than what you would get if you sold your car privately"
The sell-to-a-dealer page names no excluded vehicles, no cancellation charge and no right to revise an offer after inspection, so none of it can be checked up front
Private revenue fell 11% to £23.6m while profit from the trade auction rose 14% — the paid advert is the shrinking half of the business
Liability under the online deals and reservations terms "shall not in any circumstances exceed £0 in total"
No financial regulator and no ombudsman over a used car sale — escalation means the dealer or the courts
Autotrader's own safety guide tells private sellers to "always meet potential buyers at your home"
No refunds or credits if your advert is pulled for breaching the advertising guidelines
verdict: Take the free dealer auction if you want the car gone, the money certain and the weekend back: £0 to sell, over 5,000 trade buyers bidding, free collection and same-day payment inside 48 hours is the strongest no-cost disposal route in this comparison, and Dealer Auction being a real wholesale marketplace rather than one buying desk is what makes the bidding worth having. Accept that you are selling at trade and not at the £17,131 average asking price Autotrader's own index reports, and read the offer's terms for inspection and cancellation before a lorry arrives, because the marketing page covers none of that. Pay for a private advert instead if your car is desirable, unusual or cheap enough that a few hundred pounds matters more than a fortnight of messages — nine million visitors a month is the biggest shop window in Britain — but insist on seeing the price for your value band before you commit, since the published table cannot be read. Either way, tell DVLA the day the car leaves and claim the full months of tax back.

faqs.q: Does it cost anything to sell my car to a dealer through Autotrader?
faqs.a: No. The sell-to-a-dealer auction is free to the seller, and that includes collection from your home and payment on the same day. Autotrader is paid by the trade: its share of profit from Dealer Auction, the wholesale marketplace it owns 49% of, was £4.1m in the year to 31 March 2026, up 14%. A private advert, by contrast, is a paid product priced by how much your car is worth.

faqs.q: How much is an Autotrader private advert?
faqs.a: We could not verify it. Autotrader prices private adverts in bands based on the vehicle's value, with different prices in Great Britain and Northern Ireland, but the price table at autotrader.co.uk/sell-my-car/advertising-prices returns "Hmm, seems there's no items to display" instead of figures, and the van equivalent is empty too. Get the price for your band on screen before you commit. The one documented detail is that the package keeping an advert live until the car sells is only offered to private sellers.

faqs.q: Will I get less selling to a dealer than selling privately?
faqs.a: Yes, and Autotrader says as much. Its part-exchange pages explain that a dealer's valuation "will be slightly less than what you would get if you sold your car privately" because the dealer carries the stocking and preparation costs before reselling. Its August 2026 index put the average used car asking price at £17,131 with cars taking 30 days to sell — both of those are the dealer's costs, not your proceeds.

faqs.q: What do I have to do about tax and the DVLA?
faqs.a: Tell DVLA as soon as the car changes hands. Your vehicle tax is then cancelled and you get a refund for any full months remaining, so a sale early in the month costs you the rest of it. The tax does not transfer to the buyer, who must tax the car before driving it. Until DVLA's record changes you remain the registered keeper, which means any fines follow you.

faqs.q: Is a private car sale regulated?
faqs.a: No. There is no Financial Conduct Authority permission over selling a used car and no ombudsman scheme to escalate to, and the Consumer Rights Act protects buyers from traders rather than from private individuals. What has changed is the law on dealers pretending otherwise: since 6 April 2025, paragraph 25 of Schedule 20 to the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 bans a trader from "falsely representing oneself as a consumer" in all circumstances.

If you have never changed a wishbone before, the instructions for your exact model are there before you have spent anything.
