sections.heading: Four blocks of cover, and the point at which each one stops
sections.html:
Roadside Assistance is the base. A patrol attends anywhere in the UK more than a quarter of a mile from the address on your membership, and call-outs are unlimited. Parts worth up to £5 are fitted free; anything dearer is charged. At Home closes the quarter-mile gap, covering the registered address and the surrounding quarter of a mile, with recovery to a nearby garage if the car cannot be fixed on the drive.

National Recovery takes the driver, the vehicle and up to seven passengers to any single destination in the UK when a roadside repair is not possible. Onward Travel deals with the rest of the day: a mid-range saloon or hatchback hire car for up to 72 hours, or one night of bed and breakfast at a hotel the AA picks, or the cost of a train, bus or coach for the driver and seven passengers to where they were going. Taxis are not paid for, and Onward Travel is limited to three claims in any one membership year.

Three add-ons sit outside the recovery service. Parts and Garage Cover pays up to £535 per claim towards parts, labour and VAT with a £35 excess, after a 14-day wait, capped at five paid claims in 12 months (six on multi-vehicle joint or family membership). Tyre Cover pays up to £160 per tyre. Key Cover is sold separately and also carries a 14-day wait. Any vehicle on the policy must be under 3.5 tonnes, no more than 2.55 metres wide and 7 metres long — petrol, diesel, electric or hydrogen, of any age, including vans, minibuses, motorhomes and motorcycles.

sections.heading: Buying it round the person instead of the car
sections.html:
The choice that changes the price most is not the tier but the basis. Vehicle cover attaches to one registration and travels with the car whoever is driving it. Personal cover attaches to you and works in any eligible vehicle, as driver or as passenger, which is the version worth paying for if you regularly drive a partner's car, a parent's car or a borrowed one.

Personal membership can be taken for one person, extended to a second on joint cover, or stretched to three further household members — all of whom must live at the same address. A hire car is covered only with the rental company's permission, and a fleet of three or more vehicles has to move to the AA's commercial product rather than sit on a personal membership.

sections.heading: Who is actually standing behind each promise
sections.html:
One membership number hides five companies. Automobile Association Insurance Services Limited, firm reference 310562, arranges everything. The recovery services themselves — Roadside, At Home and National Recovery — come from Automobile Association Developments Limited, trading as AA Breakdown Services, with AA Underwriting Insurance Company Limited providing part of the Roadside element. Onward Travel and Parts and Garage Cover are insurance policies underwritten by Acromas Insurance Company Limited, authorised by the Financial Services Commission in Gibraltar and operating from a UK branch at Enbrook Park, Sandgate, Folkestone. Tyre Cover is underwritten by Astrenska Insurance Limited, trading as Collinson Insurance.

The group behind them was taken off the London market in a buyout completed on 29 March 2021 by TowerBrook Capital Partners and Warburg Pincus, with Stonepeak joining as an investor in December 2023. The accounts for the year to 31 January 2026 show revenue of £1,505m, adjusted EBITDA of £481m and net debt of £1,906m, with average income per member reported at around £200. A debt pile close to four times earnings is not a reason to avoid the AA, but it is the commercial pressure that sits behind renewal pricing, and it is a matter of public record rather than speculation.

sections.heading: The Ombudsman cannot look at most of what you have bought
sections.html:
This is the part of AA membership least understood by the people buying it, and it is not the AA's invention — it follows from the fact that a recovery service is a service contract, not a contract of insurance. The Financial Ombudsman Service says so on its own site: "We can't look into every complaint we get because of the way breakdown cover is regulated. Some businesses may carry out unregulated services and we can only look at complaints about services that are regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority." It then names the products it cannot review — policy pricing, call-outs, roadside repairs and vehicle recovery — and adds, in terms: "We can't look into complaints about these issues if you're with AA, RAC or some other smaller providers."

What remains inside the Ombudsman's reach is the insured part: onward travel, repairs at a garage, overnight accommodation and incidents in Europe. So a dispute over a £535 Parts and Garage claim or an unpaid hotel bill has a free, independent route of appeal. A dispute about a patrol taking four hours, or a recovery refused as a recurring fault, or the price you were charged, does not. Complain to the AA, and if that fails the remaining options are the courts or your card provider. Anyone choosing between providers on the strength of an ombudsman backstop should know that on the headline service the backstop is not there, for the AA or for its main rivals.

sections.heading: Year two is where the real price lives
sections.html:
The 40% sale discount is explicit about its limits: online only, until 31 August 2026, new customers, first year, and only on packages that include At Home, National Recovery or Onward Travel. Roadside Assistance on its own, Parts and Garage Cover, Key Cover, Tyre Cover and Commercial Use are all excluded from it. Whatever you pay in year one, year two starts from an undiscounted base.

Ordinarily a renewing customer would be protected by the FCA's pricing rules, which since 1 January 2022 have required that a renewal quote is no higher than the price the same customer would be given as a new customer through the same channel. Those rules are written for home and motor insurance. Standalone breakdown cover is neither, so the equal-pricing protection does not apply to it, and neither does the Ombudsman — as above, pricing is one of the things it cannot examine. The practical protection is the notice period: annual members get a renewal notice before the second year begins, and monthly members must be told of a payment change at least 45 days in advance. Both are worth diarising, because on this product the only person checking the renewal price against a new-customer quote is you.

sections.heading: Charges and conditions that catch people out
sections.html:
Most cover cannot be used until 24 hours after purchase, so it is no use buying it at the roadside; Parts and Garage Cover and Key Cover need 14 days. A fault that recurs within 28 days is not covered unless the car went to a garage for permanent repair and you can show evidence of it, and repeated claims for the same problem may push the premium up. Misfuelling is not a breakdown: the AA offers a Fuel Assist service you pay for. Lost keys are the same story — locksmith costs are excluded unless Key Cover is on the policy. Breakdowns involving the emergency services after an accident, and routine maintenance, sit outside the membership altogether.

Parts and Garage Cover excludes service items, body panels, glass, keys, air conditioning unless its failure caused the breakdown, pre-existing faults, contaminated fuel damage and wear items including brake pads and clutch friction surfaces — which between them account for a good share of what actually fails on an older car. On the administrative side there is a £20 adjustment fee to cancel an unused annual policy inside the 14-day cooling-off period, 30 days' notice to come off continuous cover, £2 for a replacement card and £15 for a written VAT notification.

pros: 2,753 directly employed patrols, the largest force in the UK, attending 3.5 million breakdowns a year
8 in 10 cars repaired at the roadside on the AA's own April 2025 to March 2026 data, with a target of arriving inside the hour
Unlimited call-outs on every tier, with no annual cap on the number of attendances
Defaqto 5 Star expert rating on Roadside with National Recovery, At Home and Onward Travel
Personal cover follows you into any eligible vehicle as driver or passenger, and can carry three extra household members
Every patrol trained to Level 1 for electric vehicles and more than 98% to Level 2
No upper age limit on the vehicle, and vans, motorhomes, minibuses and motorcycles all qualify within the weight and size limits
cons: The Financial Ombudsman Service states it cannot investigate complaints about call-outs, roadside repairs, vehicle recovery or policy pricing for AA members, because those services sit outside FCA regulation — only onward travel, garage repairs, accommodation and European incidents are within its reach
The FCA's equal-pricing rule for renewals covers home and motor insurance, not standalone breakdown cover, so nothing obliges the AA to match its new-customer price at renewal
The 40% discount is first-year and new-customer only, excludes Roadside-only membership and every add-on, and ends 31 August 2026
A fault that returns within 28 days is not covered without documented evidence of a permanent garage repair, which puts the burden of proof on the member
Parts and Garage Cover pays a maximum of £535 per claim with a £35 excess and excludes wear items such as brake pads and clutch friction surfaces — much of what fails on a high-mileage car
Onward Travel is capped at three claims a year, one night's accommodation and 72 hours of hire car, and taxis are never paid for
Cancelling an unused annual policy in the cooling-off period still costs a £20 adjustment fee, and continuous cover needs 30 days' notice to stop
verdict: If what you want is the best chance of being fixed where you stand rather than towed to a garage, the AA is the strongest argument in the market: 2,753 of its own patrols, 3.5 million attendances a year and 8 in 10 cars repaired at the roadside. Bought in a sale with At Home and National Recovery attached, the first year is competitive with providers running a fraction of that capacity. The reservations are about what happens afterwards rather than what happens at the roadside — the discount is first-year only, the renewal price is not governed by the FCA rule that protects home and motor customers, and the Ombudsman cannot examine a dispute about a call-out, a recovery or a price. Treat it as a service you re-shop every year and it is very good value. Treat it as a subscription you never look at again and it will quietly cost you more than it should.

faqs.q: How soon can I use AA cover after buying it?
faqs.a: Most of the membership becomes usable 24 hours after purchase, so it cannot be bought at the side of the road to deal with a breakdown already in progress. Parts and Garage Cover and Key Cover both carry a longer 14-day wait before a claim can be made.

faqs.q: Does the AA cover a breakdown on my own driveway?
faqs.a: Only with At Home added. Standard Roadside Assistance excludes breakdowns at the registered address and within the surrounding quarter of a mile. At Home covers that area and will recover the vehicle to a nearby garage if it cannot be repaired where it sits.

faqs.q: Can I take a complaint about a slow patrol to the Financial Ombudsman?
faqs.a: No. The Ombudsman's own guidance says it cannot look into complaints about call-outs, roadside repairs, vehicle recovery or policy pricing where the provider is the AA or the RAC, because those services are not regulated by the FCA. It can consider complaints about onward travel, repairs carried out at a garage, overnight accommodation and incidents in Europe.

faqs.q: What does Onward Travel actually pay for?
faqs.a: One of three things, arranged by the AA rather than chosen by you: a mid-range saloon or hatchback hire car for up to 72 hours, one night's bed and breakfast at a hotel of the AA's choosing, or public transport for the driver and up to seven passengers to the intended destination. Taxis are excluded, and the benefit is limited to three claims in a membership year.

faqs.q: Will my price go up at renewal?
faqs.a: It can. Any introductory discount applies to the first year for new customers only, and the FCA rule requiring renewal prices to match new-customer prices applies to home and motor insurance rather than standalone breakdown cover. Annual members receive a renewal notice, and monthly members must be given at least 45 days' notice of a change to payments — both are the moment to compare against a fresh quote.

faqs.q: Which vehicles can go on the policy?
faqs.a: Petrol, diesel, electric and hydrogen cars of any age, plus vans, minibuses, motorhomes and motorcycles, provided each is under 3.5 tonnes gross weight, no more than 2.55 metres wide excluding mirrors and no more than 7 metres long. A caravan or trailer being towed at the time is covered within the same limits.

title: AA Motorbike Insurance (Europa Bike) Review
meta_title: AA Motorbike Insurance Review: Cover, Fees and Who Runs It
meta_description: AA-badged bike cover is arranged by Europa Bike: the five-insurer panel, a £20m third-party limit, the full fee list and what the policy leaves out.
intro:
The AA badge on a motorbike policy has always belonged to somebody else: Europa Bike, a Bristol broker that has done nothing but two-wheeled insurance since 1996. Companies House has the firm as Europa Group Limited, number 03279177, incorporated on 15 November 1996 under its original name of Motor Cycle Direct Insurance Services Limited and renamed on 3 December 2003. Its terms of business set out a panel of five insurers for annual motorbike policies — Highway, Aviva, Tradex, Ageas and AXA — and since 1 August 2023 every policy has carried basic legal expenses cover at no extra charge.

That specialism is the reason four household names put their own badge on Europa's paperwork. The group has arranged bike cover behind AA Motorcycle Insurance and RAC Bike Insurance, and motor cover behind Ford Insure and Vauxhall Insurance, alongside its own brands Motorcycle Direct, Onequote Direct, Ridersure and Wiser Choice. One thing has changed and it matters if you came here from a search for the AA: the AA's own motorbike page now reads “we’re sorry, the AA is no longer offering insurance for motorbikes”, followed by “if you’re an existing policyholder don’t worry – you’re still covered” and “AA Motorbike Insurance is provided by Europa Bike.” The book did not lapse; it simply lost the badge, and Europa Bike runs it directly.

What sits underneath is a straightforward specialist motor policy. Third-party property damage is covered to £20,000,000 against a statutory minimum of £1,200,000, the claims line on 0344 335 2934 is staffed 24 hours a day, and no claims bonus builds to nine years. Comprehensive, third party fire and theft, third party only and a laid-up option for a bike off the road are all sold, and the current policy booklet carries the version stamp FEB26(V), so the wording is being maintained rather than left to age.

sections.heading: One Bristol broker, four familiar badges
sections.html:
Europa Group trades from Unit 2, West Point Row, Great Park Road, Bradley Stoke, Bristol BS32 4QG, and is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority under firm reference 309794 — a number you can check yourself on the FCA Register. The group describes six brands of its own: Motorcycle Direct for bikes and scooters sold direct, Onequote Direct for car, van and home, Ridersure for brokers, Europa Underwriting, Wiser Choice and Wiser Choice Bike. On top of those it has run white-label programmes for the AA, the RAC, Ford and Vauxhall, and says Ford Insure alone delivered more than 500,000 policies over five years.

The AA-branded paperwork is still hosted on Europa's own servers, which is how the arrangement is visible from outside. The legal expenses wording issued with AA bike policies carries the reference LEI/AA/06/19 and names two further firms: 4th Dimension Innovation Limited of Thorpe Business Park, Egham (firm reference 516498) as administrator, and Financial and Legal Insurance Company Limited of Cheadle (firm reference 202915) as insurer. That wording covers uninsured loss recovery to £100,000 with solicitors' costs capped at £100 an hour, motor prosecution defence to £2,500, and requires a claim to be reported within 120 days of the incident. The AA page itself refers to policies purchased or renewed from 10 September 2020.

A small inconsistency is worth knowing about before you go looking for the company. The terms of business dated August 2024 still give the address as Europa House, Midland Way, Thornbury, Bristol BS35 2JX. Companies House and the current website footer both give the Bradley Stoke address. The registered number and firm reference are identical in both, so this is a move that one document has yet to catch up with rather than two different companies.

sections.heading: What the policy pays on, and where it stops
sections.html:
Liability for injury to other people is unlimited, as the Road Traffic Act requires; damage to their property is covered to £20,000,000, which is a little over sixteen times the £1,200,000 the law actually demands. Comprehensive adds accidental damage, spare parts and accessories, and recovery of the bike to the nearest approved repairer. Third party fire and theft strips that back to fire and theft losses. The laid-up option covers fire, theft and accidental damage only while the bike sits at the garaging address you declared, and drops the requirement for tax and an MOT.

New motorcycle replacement is one of the better clauses and one of the most conditional. It applies where the bike is stolen, or where repair costs run past 70% of its list price including VAT, within six months of purchase — and only if you were the first registered owner and own the bike outright or on hire purchase. Leasing and contract hire are outside it. Otherwise the settlement basis is market value, the agreed figure on your schedule or the cost of repair, whichever is lowest.

Riding abroad is allowed for 30 days per trip up to 90 days in any one period of insurance, across the EU and designated countries. No claims bonus runs to nine years with protection available, and the booklet publishes the full step-back table for up to three fault claims. The exclusions are the ordinary ones for the class: helmets, leathers and personal belongings are not covered by the policy itself, theft is excluded where the keys were left in the ignition, and unauthorised use by someone known to you is excluded unless you report it to the police. Defence costs after a death on the road are capped at £1,000 for any one occurrence, which is modest next to the £2,500 in the separate legal expenses wording.

sections.heading: Six add-ons, and what each one is worth
sections.html:
Because the core policy leaves out protective kit and most of the legal cost of an accident, the optional list is where a lot of the value sits:

  • Legal expenses: up to £100,000 for non-fault claims, including personal injury and motoring defence. The basic version has been included free on policies since 1 August 2023.
  • Helmet and leathers: up to £1,000 for protective gear damaged in an accident — the gap the main policy leaves.
  • Personal accident: up to £25,000 for injury, disability or death.
  • Replacement vehicle: a hire bike of up to 650cc for up to 14 days after an accident, theft or vandalism.
  • Excess Protect: refunds the excess up to £600 a year on accidental damage, fire, theft, vandalism and flood claims.
  • Key Protect: up to £1,500 towards locksmiths and immobiliser reprogramming for lost, stolen or broken keys.

Discounts are offered for no claims history, secure parking and riding experience. Europa is paid a flat fee by the insurer for arranging the optional extras, which is disclosed in the terms of business rather than buried.

sections.heading: The fee schedule, in full
sections.html:
This is a non-advised sale: the terms of business say plainly “you will not receive advice or a recommendation from us”, and the firm acts as your agent in arranging the insurance while acting as the insurer's agent when collecting premiums and paying refunds. Premiums are treated as held by the insurer under risk transfer, and any interest earned on them is kept by Europa Group. Commission is taken from the insurer as a percentage that varies with the bike and the rider, plus a percentage of the loan where the premium is paid monthly through the group's credit provider.

The charges published in the August 2024 document are:

  • Renewal: up to £75
  • Mid-term change: £40 through the contact centre, £20 through the online portal
  • Cancelling inside the 14-day cooling-off period: £40
  • Cancelling after it, where the policy came from a price comparison site: £75
  • Cancelling after it, where it did not: £40
  • Policy voided for misrepresentation: £75
  • Duplicate documents: £10
  • Correcting a new business error: free

Paying monthly costs more than paying in one go, which the document states rather than leaving you to work out. The cooling-off period runs 14 days from the start of the policy or the day you receive the documents, whichever is later. Europa Group is covered by both the Financial Ombudsman Service and the Financial Services Compensation Scheme, and takes complaints at crt@europa-group.co.uk.

sections.heading: Its own complaints numbers are published, and they are not flattering
sections.html:
Europa Group publishes its complaints return on its own website, which most brokers do not, and the figures for 1 January to 30 June 2026 are worth reading before you buy. It opened 215 complaints and closed 209. Of those, 102 were closed inside three days and 107 took longer than three days but under eight weeks. None took more than eight weeks, which is a genuinely good result. But 44% were upheld — the firm agreed the customer was right in nearly half the cases it decided — and the total redress paid on all upheld complaints was £3,562, against £1,221 paid out on complaints it rejected. Spread across roughly 92 upheld cases, that is an average of about £39 each.

For scale, the Financial Ombudsman Service's annual data published on 21 May 2026 recorded 13,420 new complaints about car or motorcycle insurance in 2025/26, upheld at 35%, within 214,600 complaints across all financial products at an average uphold rate of 30%. A 44% uphold rate at the firm's own first stage sits above that, though the two are not measuring quite the same thing: a broker's internal figure counts service and administration disputes that never reach the ombudsman.

The wider value picture comes from the FCA's general insurance value measures data for calendar year 2025, published on 21 July 2026. Motor claims costs rose to 59% of premium from 54% the year before while premiums fell 7% and policies in force grew 4%, and the motor claims acceptance rate stands at 99%. Motorcycle is not itemised separately in that release, so there is no bike-specific acceptance rate to hold any insurer against.

sections.heading: The risk the premium is actually pricing
sections.html:
Bike premiums look punishing next to car premiums until you look at the casualty rates. The Department for Transport's motorcyclist factsheet, published on 30 July 2026, records 386 motorcyclists killed on Britain's roads in 2025 and 5,710 seriously injured, 6,096 killed or seriously injured in total. The fatality rate works out at 128 per billion vehicle miles and the serious injury rate at 1,891. Across 2021 to 2025, 92% of motorcycle KSI casualties were male and 62% of fatalities happened away from junctions on rural roads. The rate has improved — down 37% across all severities since 2004 — but it remains an order of magnitude above car travel.

Demand is going the other way. Motorcycle Industry Association registrations to May 2026 were running 15.8% ahead of the same point in 2025, with adventure bikes up 24.8% year to date and road sport up 16.9%. Meanwhile the Association of British Insurers reported on 29 July 2026 that insurers paid a record £3.2 billion in motor claims in the second quarter, with the average claim up 4% to £4,900 and the average motor premium paid rising £6 to £566. More riders, dearer repairs and a casualty rate like that is the arithmetic behind every bike quote you will be given this year.

pros: Motorcycle-only specialist since 1996, and the firm actually behind AA, RAC, Ford and Vauxhall-badged cover
Third-party property damage to £20,000,000, against a legal minimum of £1,200,000
Basic legal expenses cover included free on policies since 1 August 2023
Claims line staffed 24 hours a day, seven days a week
Not one complaint took longer than eight weeks to close in the first half of 2026
Laid-up cover available for a bike off the road, without needing tax or an MOT
New motorcycle replacement within six months where repairs pass 70% of list price
cons: The AA has stopped selling motorbike insurance altogether, and the Europa Bike site now leads to a customer portal for existing policyholders rather than a quote form — new riders are pushed towards the group's Motorcycle Direct brand instead
44% of the 209 complaints closed between January and June 2026 were upheld, and the total redress paid on them came to £3,562, an average of roughly £39
No excess figures appear in the policy booklet or the summary document — the wording says only that the amount is shown on your schedule, so you cannot compare it before you quote
The fee schedule is steep for a bike policy: up to £75 to renew, £75 to cancel if you bought through a price comparison site, £40 for a phone amendment and £10 for a duplicate document
Helmets, leathers and personal belongings are excluded from the policy itself and only covered by buying the £1,000 add-on
No sales or service telephone number is published — contact runs through live chat, Monday to Friday 9am to 6pm and Saturday 9am to 1pm
The published documents are out of step with each other: a summary dated August 2023, terms of business from August 2024 carrying a superseded Thornbury address, and a booklet stamped FEB26(V)
verdict: Europa Bike is a competent motorcycle specialist that has spent three decades doing one thing, and the policy behind the AA badge is a reasonable one: a £20,000,000 third-party limit, a five-insurer panel, free basic legal cover and a 24-hour claims line. The catch is that the badge has gone. The AA no longer sells bike insurance, Europa Bike's own site now serves existing policyholders rather than new ones, and a rider looking for a fresh quote from this firm needs its Motorcycle Direct brand instead. Existing AA policyholders are still covered and should read the fee list before their renewal lands: at up to £75 to renew and £75 to cancel, the administration can move the price as much as the risk does.

faqs.q: Can I still buy AA motorbike insurance?
faqs.a: No. The AA's own motorbike page states that it is no longer offering insurance for motorbikes. Existing policies remain in force and Europa Bike, which arranged them, now looks after the book directly. If you want a new quote from the same firm, it sells under its Motorcycle Direct brand.

faqs.q: Who underwrites the cover?
faqs.a: Europa Group Limited is a broker, not an insurer. Its terms of business name a panel of five insurers for annual motorbike policies: Highway, Aviva, Tradex, Ageas and AXA. The policy booklet does not name the insurer at all, referring only to “the insurer described in your schedule”, so you will not know which of the five you have until the documents arrive.

faqs.q: What is the excess?
faqs.a: It is not published. Both the policy booklet and the insurance product information document confirm that an excess applies but state the amount is shown on your individual schedule. Ask for it in writing before you accept a quote, and ask separately about any additional excess for young or newly qualified riders.

faqs.q: How long can I ride abroad on the policy?
faqs.a: Thirty days per trip, up to a maximum of 90 days in any one period of insurance, across Great Britain, Northern Ireland, the Channel Islands, the Isle of Man and EU or designated countries.

faqs.q: Is Europa Bike properly regulated?
faqs.a: Europa Group Limited is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority under firm reference 309794 and registered in England and Wales as company 03279177. It is covered by both the Financial Ombudsman Service and the Financial Services Compensation Scheme. The firm reference is verifiable on the FCA Register.

faqs.q: What does it cost to change or cancel a policy?
faqs.a: The August 2024 terms of business set a mid-term change at £40 through the contact centre or £20 online, cancellation at £40 inside the 14-day cooling-off period, £40 afterwards, or £75 afterwards if the policy came from a price comparison site. A voided policy costs £75 and duplicate documents £10. Insurer charges may apply on top.

title: AA Van Insurance Review
meta_title: AA Van Insurance Review: Cover, Fees and Its 4 Insurers
meta_description: The AA arranges van cover from four named insurers. What its own contract document says about fees, class of use and the price promise at renewal.
intro:
Van insurance from the AA is arranged by Automobile Association Insurance Services Limited, a broker holding Financial Conduct Authority firm reference 310562, verifiable on the FCA Register. It is a big operation by any measure. The company's own published complaints statement counts 2,763,187 insurance policies sold in the six months from 1 August 2025 to 31 January 2026, and its filed accounts for the year to 31 January 2025 show revenue of £295m, up from £265m the year before.

The useful thing about the AA on vans is that it names its underwriters in writing. Its van contract document, dated July 2025, lists a panel of four: Ageas Insurance Limited, Aviva Insurance Limited, Covéa Insurance plc and Highway Insurance Company Limited. Whichever of those four prices your risk is printed on the quote before you buy, which is more than most van sites will tell you. Comprehensive cover comes with windscreen repair or replacement that does not cost you your no claims discount, an uninsured driver promise that waives the excess and protects the discount if an identified uninsured driver hits you, personal belongings cover and a UK claims line open around the clock on 0330 053 0322.

Sitting over the top of all four is the AA's Fair Price Promise: "When it's time to renew, we promise you won't pay more than if you were a new customer." For a van that phrase carries more weight than it does on a car, for a reason set out further down this page. Cover runs from third party only through third party, fire and theft to comprehensive, drivers aged 18 to 99 are eligible, and up to four additional named drivers can go on the policy. A quote holds for 28 days and cover can be bought up to 30 days before it starts.

sections.heading: Four insurers behind one badge, and what each of them brings
sections.html:
The AA does not carry the risk on a van policy. It finds an insurer, sets the policy up and administers it, and takes a share of the premium for doing so. Its van contract document says plainly that the firm is "not able to provide you with a personal recommendation on which insurance or optional additional products you should purchase", and that it acts for the insurer rather than for you: "We act for our insurer(s) in marketing their products and we are authorised to act for the insurer when entering into a contract of insurance with you on their behalf." Premium and claims money is handled as the insurer's agent, which is the arrangement that protects you if the broker fails before the money reaches the underwriter.

Knowing the four names lets you read the actual cover before you buy. Highway Insurance Company Limited publishes its van product document under FCA reference 202972, and the numbers in it are the numbers you would be buying: third-party injury cover unlimited, third-party property damage up to £5,000,000, personal accident benefit of £5,000 for the policyholder and partner, personal belongings up to £300, replacement locks up to £500, non-factory-fitted in-vehicle equipment up to £500, and audio equipment capped at £150 on third party, fire and theft. Driving abroad runs to 37 European countries at the minimum cover the law there requires, not the comprehensive cover you hold at home. Theft is not paid if the van was left unlocked, or with the keys in it and the engine running — the single exclusion that catches more multi-drop drivers than any other.

sections.heading: The three fees, and where in the price each one hides
sections.html:
The AA's van contract document sets out the charges in one place, which not every broker does. A £28 arrangement fee is "included in the agreed price", so it does not appear as a separate line and it is already inside the figure on the quote. A £25 admin fee applies to any policy change made over the phone or through webchat, and no fee at all applies to the same change made in the online account — a genuine saving for anyone who changes a registration or an address more than once a year. Cancelling costs £32.50.

The cooling-off period is 14 days from the later of receiving the documents or entering the contract. Inside it, a policy that has not started yet gets a full premium refund; one that has started gets the premium back less a deduction for the days on cover. The fees are kept either way, and a policy with a claim on it gets nothing back. The Financial Services Compensation Scheme covers the arranging of van insurance at 90% of a claim with no upper limit, and the compulsory third-party element in full.

If a claim goes wrong, complaints go to Customer Solutions, The AA, Park Square, Birdhall Lane, Cheadle SK3 0XN, or to 0344 209 0556, and then to the Financial Ombudsman Service. That last step is worth a moment. In the Ombudsman's annual data published 21 May 2026, covering 214,600 new complaints across every financial product at an average uphold rate of 30%, commercial vehicle insurance produced 1,429 complaints and the Ombudsman found for the customer in 44% of them — against 35% on car and motorcycle policies, from 13,420 complaints. Van disputes are the ones the Ombudsman is most likely to decide against the insurer.

sections.heading: Class of use decides the price, the cover and the rules that apply
sections.html:
The AA offers three classes: social, domestic and commuting; carriage of own goods; and haulage. Picking the wrong one is the most common way a van claim is refused, because carrying anything for payment on a social-and-commuting policy is uninsured driving. Carriage of own goods covers tools and stock belonging to your own business. Haulage covers goods belonging to somebody else, and prices accordingly.

That choice has a second consequence almost nobody flags. The FCA's pricing rules, in force since 1 January 2022, stop an insurer charging a renewing customer more than an equivalent new customer. They apply to consumer home and motor policies, and the FCA extended them to owners of commercial vehicles such as vans and pickups only where the vehicle is used for social, domestic and pleasure purposes. A van insured for carriage of own goods or haulage sits outside them. Pick either of the business classes and the legal protection against a walk-up renewal price disappears — which is exactly why the AA's Fair Price Promise is worth reading properly on a van. On a business-use van it is not the regulator's floor being restated. It is a voluntary commitment doing a job no rule is doing, and it is the strongest single argument for the AA over a cheaper name that makes no such promise.

Some context for what is being priced. SMMT's Motorparc figures published 24 April 2026 put 5,175,598 vans on UK roads at the end of 2025, up 1.4% in the year and up 29.2% since 2015 — faster growth than any other vehicle type. Battery electric vans passed 113,256, or 2.2% of the fleet. The ABI's motor figures published 29 July 2026 show insurers paying a record £3.2bn in claims in the second quarter of 2026, an average premium of £566, an average claim of £4,900 and windscreen repairs alone averaging £283. Against a £4,900 average claim, choosing a £500 voluntary excess to shave the premium is a real bet, not a formality.

sections.heading: What the add-ons actually pay for
sections.html:
Four extras can be bolted on. Van Legal Assistance pursues uninsured losses — the excess, lost earnings, injury — that the motor policy itself will not pay. Van Hire provides a replacement for up to 28 days, limited to two claims in a policy year, which is the add-on that matters most if the van is how you earn. Tools in Transit also allows two claims a year, sharing one combined limit between them; the limit is set at quote and is worth checking against what is genuinely in the back, because a full plumber's or sparks' kit outruns a typical cap quickly. Breakdown Cover is capped at three call-outs a policy year, which is a meaningfully thinner product than the AA's standalone membership, where roadside call-outs are unlimited. Anyone buying an AA van policy mainly to get AA recovery should price the membership separately rather than assume the add-on is the same thing.

Two discounts are worth asking about. A GPS tracker can take up to 10% off, and a higher voluntary excess — selectable up to £500 — will move the price, though the insurer's compulsory excess sits underneath it and can rise again for younger drivers or heavier vehicles.

sections.heading: Three things to weigh before you click through
sections.html:
The first is the size of the panel. Four insurers is a narrow shortlist for a market this large, and it is narrow by the AA's own standards — its car contract document runs to roughly 13 insurers. A four-name panel will not always find the cheapest van premium, and since the sale is non-advised nobody at the AA will tell you when it has not. Running the same details through a broader panel before committing costs nothing but time.

The second is the evidence gap on this specific product. The AA publishes a Defaqto 5 Star rating for Gold and Platinum comprehensive car insurance and for Platinum home insurance, and quotes a hard price benchmark for car — 10% of customers paying £265 or less, on new business from February to July 2026. There is no published Defaqto rating for AA van insurance and no equivalent van price figure on the site. The AA's own complaints table for the period is loaded by script and does not render as text, so the complaint volumes and uphold rates behind that 2,763,187 policy count could not be read directly and need confirming with the AA. The FCA's value measures data published 21 July 2026 covers motor as a whole — a 99% claims acceptance rate and claims costs at 59% of premium, up from 54% — but does not break vans out, so there is no van-specific acceptance rate to hold any of the four insurers against.

The third is that one of the four underwriters is about to change its name. Highway Insurance Company Limited is one of the entities transferring into Allianz Insurance plc under a Part VII scheme of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000, with a High Court sanction hearing listed for 2 October 2026 and an effective date of 1 January 2027. Policy terms carry across a Part VII transfer unchanged and there is nothing for a policyholder to do, but anyone quoted on Highway should expect the Allianz name on their renewal and should read the scheme documents if they want the detail rather than the summary.

pros: Names all four panel insurers in writing, so the underwriter and its published limits can be checked before buying
Fair Price Promise caps the renewal at the new-customer price, which matters most on business-use vans that FCA pricing rules do not cover
Windscreen repair or replacement without losing the no claims discount, on comprehensive
Uninsured driver promise refunds the excess and protects the discount where the other driver is identified and uninsured
Policy changes made in the online account carry no admin fee, against £25 by phone or webchat
Haulage as well as carriage of own goods is quoted, which several direct insurers will not touch
Up to 10% off where a GPS tracker is fitted, and four named drivers included
Wide eligibility: drivers from 18 to 99, with UK, EU or foreign licences accepted
cons: Only four insurers on the van panel, against roughly 13 on the AA's own car panel, so the cheapest van premium in the market will often sit outside it
The sale is non-advised and the AA acts as agent of the insurer, not of you, so nobody is obliged to tell you the panel has been beaten elsewhere

£28 arrangement fee is folded into the quoted price rather than shown separately, £25 to change anything by phone or webchat, £32.50 to cancel — and all of it is kept even if you cancel inside the 14-day cooling-off period
No published Defaqto rating and no van price benchmark, while AA car and home insurance get both
Breakdown as an add-on is capped at three call-outs a year, far thinner than the unlimited roadside call-outs on standalone AA membership
Highway policyholders will see their underwriter become Allianz Insurance plc on 1 January 2027 under a Part VII transfer
Commercial vehicle insurance carries a 44% Ombudsman uphold rate against 35% for cars, so van claims disputes are more often decided against the insurer
verdict: The AA is a broker on vans, not an insurer, and it is unusually straight about it — the four panel insurers are named, the three fees are written down, and the basis of sale is spelled out. That transparency is the reason to start here. The Fair Price Promise is the strongest part of the offer and is worth more on a van than on a car, because a van insured for carriage of own goods or haulage sits outside the FCA rules that would otherwise cap a renewal. Set against that, four insurers is a short panel, the fees are real and non-refundable, and there is no van-specific quality rating to check. Worth a quote, particularly for own-goods and haulage use, and worth putting a broader panel alongside it before you buy.

faqs.q: Who underwrites AA van insurance?
faqs.a: One of four insurers named in the AA's van contract document dated July 2025: Ageas Insurance Limited, Aviva Insurance Limited, Covéa Insurance plc or Highway Insurance Company Limited. Which one you get is shown on the quote before you buy. Highway is transferring into Allianz Insurance plc on 1 January 2027 under a Part VII scheme, with a sanction hearing listed for 2 October 2026.

faqs.q: What does the AA charge in fees on a van policy?
faqs.a: A £28 arrangement fee is built into the quoted price rather than added on top. Changing the policy costs £25 by phone or webchat and nothing through the online account. Cancelling costs £32.50. Inside the 14-day cooling-off period the premium is refunded in full if cover has not started, or less a charge for time on cover if it has, but the fees are kept in both cases.

faqs.q: Does the Fair Price Promise apply to a business-use van?
faqs.a: The AA states the promise without carving out business use: "When it's time to renew, we promise you won't pay more than if you were a new customer." It is worth understanding why that matters on a van. The FCA's pricing rules, in force since 1 January 2022, reach commercial vehicles only where they are used for social, domestic and pleasure purposes, so a van rated for carriage of own goods or haulage has no regulatory protection against a higher renewal price. Confirm at the quote stage that the promise is being applied to your class of use.

faqs.q: Is the AA breakdown add-on the same as AA membership?
faqs.a: No. The van insurance add-on is limited to three call-outs in a policy year. Standalone AA breakdown membership has no cap on roadside call-outs. If recovery is the main reason for choosing the AA, price the membership on its own rather than relying on the add-on.

faqs.q: What class of use should I pick?
faqs.a: Social, domestic and commuting covers personal journeys and the trip to a single place of work, and nothing carried for payment. Carriage of own goods covers tools, stock and materials belonging to your own business. Haulage covers goods belonging to somebody else. Carrying anything for payment on a social-and-commuting policy leaves you uninsured, so pick up rather than down.

faqs.q: Where do I complain if a van claim goes wrong?
faqs.a: First to the AA, on 0344 209 0556, by email to insurance.complaints@theAA.com, or in writing to Customer Solutions, The AA, Park Square, Birdhall Lane, Cheadle SK3 0XN. If that does not resolve it, the Financial Ombudsman Service will look at it free of charge. Ombudsman data published on 21 May 2026 shows commercial vehicle complaints upheld at 44%, above the 30% average across all financial products.

title: The Battery Guys Vehicle Parts
meta_title: The Battery Guys: 4-Year Warranty, and the Exclusions
meta_description: A Skelmersdale battery seller trading since 1994, with a 4-year premium warranty. The Stop-Start exclusion and the 25% restocking fee are the clauses to read.

headline.label: Warranty
headline.value: 4 years on the premium range, 2 on standard, 1 on mobility and leisure

disclosure: we earn a commission if you buy through the link on this page. It costs you nothing. The warranty exclusions, the 25% restocking fee and the contradictions we found on the site are reported as published, whether they help the sale or not.
intro:
The Battery Guys is the real thing: a British company, trading as Dynamic Battery Services Limited, Companies House number 02902484, registered at Gorsey Place, Skelmersdale, and incorporated on 25 February 1994. Thirty-two years selling batteries from Lancashire, and still active.

The warranties are the headline and they are generous by the standards of the trade: four years on the premium car battery range, two years on standard, one year on mobility and leisure batteries. If the battery proves faulty the site says you choose the remedy — “we will replace it free of charge or refund your purchase price in full, your choice”.

Two things to read before you order, which we cover in full below: the warranty is void if a standard battery is fitted to a Stop-Start vehicle, and a return outside the window carries a 25% restocking fee.

sections.heading: What the batteries cost
sections.html:
Prices we read on 8 October 2026, with the site’s own statement that “the price that you see is the price that you pay, inclusive of VAT and delivery”:

BatteryPrice
096 Dynamic AGM car battery, 70Ah£120.00, was £134.42
096 Stop Start EFB, Rombat, 70Ah 650CCA£99.78 — out of stock when we looked
Dynamic 12v 7.2Ah VRLA (Leoch)£20.50
Dynamic 12v 22Ah mobility twin pack (Leoch)£95.43, was £99.99
Dynamic 12v 26Ah VRLA£50.00, was £63.50
Dynamic 12v 35Ah VRLA£90.50
Dynamic 12v 42Ah VRLA£112.00
Dynamic 12v 55Ah VRLA£120.00, was £132.00

The mobility range is where this shop looks strongest on price — a 12v 7.2Ah sealed battery at £20.50 delivered is competitive, and the twin pack at £95.43 saves the bother of matching a pair yourself.

One honest caveat about “inclusive of delivery”, which we come back to in a moment: it is not true for ten postcode areas.

sections.heading: The warranty, and the two clauses that void it
sections.html:
Set out plainly, the cover is:

  • Premium car batteries: 4 years
  • Standard car batteries: 2 years
  • Mobility and leisure: 1 year
  • Taxis, forklifts and lawnmowers: 12 months

Four years on a car battery is a strong offer, and the choice of a free replacement or a full refund is better than the replacement-only terms many sellers give.

Now the exclusions, because this is where warranty claims are won and lost. Cover does not apply to wear and tear, misuse or negligence — which the site spells out as over-charging, over-discharging, sulphation and under-charging — nor to a battery that failed because of a fault in the vehicle’s own charging system, nor to one that will not recover from a deep discharge, nor to one flattened by sitting unused.

Two go further than the usual list, and both are worth your attention:

One: a standard battery fitted to a Stop-Start vehicle is not covered. Stop-Start cars need an AGM or EFB battery, and fitting an ordinary flooded unit will shorten its life badly. If your car switches the engine off at traffic lights, buy the AGM or the EFB, not the standard.

Two: the battery must be the one the site’s own Battery Finder recommended. If you overrule the tool — because a forum told you a bigger battery fits, or because the recommended one was out of stock — you are outside the warranty. Use the Finder, and keep a screenshot of what it told you.

Claims start with a phone call or email, and the return has to be labelled “ACCUMULATOR” and addressed to the Warranty Department at Gillibrands Road, Skelmersdale. If the battery tests fine there is no test fee, but you pay the carriage back at cost — so a wrong guess costs you two lots of postage on something heavy.

sections.heading: Delivery: good cut-off, hard exclusions
sections.html:
The useful part first. Orders placed before 2pm Monday to Friday are dispatched the same day, deliveries run Monday to Saturday, 8am to 6pm, and weekend orders go out on Monday. A published 2pm cut-off is more than several bigger rivals offer.

Then the exclusions, and they are substantial:

  • Northern Ireland: excluded.
  • Channel Islands: excluded.
  • Highlands and Islands, and the Outer Hebrides: excluded.
  • North of the Central Scottish Belt, including Aberdeen: not possible, which the site attributes to “excessive courier costs”.
  • Ten postcode areas — HS, IM, IV, KA, KW, PA, PH, TR, ZE and AB — “will incur a £17.50 delivery fee”.

If you live in a large part of Scotland, Cornwall, the islands or Northern Ireland, read that list before you fall for a price. And note the muddle: AB — Aberdeen — appears in both lists on the same page, once as a £17.50 surcharge and once as an area that cannot be served at all. Ring and ask before ordering.

There is also a flat contradiction between that £17.50 fee and the category pages’ promise that “the price that you see is the price that you pay, inclusive of VAT and delivery”. Both statements are on the same website. For most of England and Wales the promise holds; for those ten postcodes it does not.

Saturday delivery is offered “at additional cost” with no amount published, no carrier is named anywhere — only “national companies” — and no standard delivery price or free-delivery threshold is stated.

One more thing you should know, and it cuts against the site’s own marketing: next-day delivery is not currently offered. The delivery page says only standard delivery is available, because next-day consignments were being delayed. Yet page titles across the site read “Next Day Delivery”, the FAQ carries a next-day badge and says batteries go out on a next-day service, and a category page claims next-day to 95% of the UK. The delivery page is the one that governs, so plan for standard.

sections.heading: Returns, and the 25% that catches people
sections.html:
You can cancel within 14 days of ordering, and goods must come back within “14 working days of the date that the items were delivered”. Returns need 24 hours’ notice first, so do not just put a battery in a box and post it.

Outside that window, anything they choose to accept is “subject to a 25% restocking fee”. On the £120 AGM battery above that is £30 gone. It is the highest restocking charge we found among the parts sellers we looked at, and the single most expensive clause on the site.

You pay the return postage “unless we have delivered the item to you in error”, and the terms add that they “reserve the right to charge the purchaser for the cost of return”. Non-faulty items left uncollected for three months are disposed of.

There is a timing conflict to be careful about. The Returns page gives you 14 days, but the Terms and Conditions say “any issues with the items we must be notified within 7 days of the delivery”. Seven and fourteen cannot both be the deadline. Work to seven days and you are safe under either reading — test the battery as soon as it arrives rather than leaving it in the garage until the weekend.

To its credit, there is no “no returns once fitted” clause anywhere on the site, which is unusual and in your favour.

sections.heading: Finding the right battery, and what is missing
sections.html:
Fitment runs two ways: “Find Your Vehicle” by make and model, across six categories — car, van, motorcycle, leisure, Trojan and golf — or “Choose By Battery Part Number” if you already know the code stamped on the old one. The part-number route is the reliable one, and the 096 in those listings is exactly that sort of code.

There is no registration-number lookup and no VIN search, which for batteries matters less than for brakes — the physical size, the terminal layout and the Ah and CCA ratings decide it. Read those from the battery you are replacing.

Three gaps worth stating. Payment methods are not listed in text, only as an image, with the terms referring vaguely to “a valid credit or debit card issued by a bank acceptable to us”. No Klarna or Clearpay. And no trade account or bulk discount is published, despite the company being classified at Companies House as a wholesaler of motor vehicle parts.

The contact details are untidier than they should be. We found three different phone numbers — 0330 055 2676 for sales, a mobile on 07946 337463, and an 0845 number on the warranty page that appears nowhere else — and two different addresses: Gillibrands Road on the contact page, Gorsey Place on the homepage map. Companies House matches Gorsey Place. There is no email address, only a form, and no opening hours.

Finally, a real gap rather than an untidy one. We could not find any published battery take-back or recycling scheme. The Safety page covers handling — eye protection, ignition sources, vent caps — and gives no disposal guidance at all, and nothing on the FAQ or terms pages addresses it either. We are reporting what is absent from the site, not what the company does behind the scenes. In the meantime, the garage fitting your battery will normally take the old one, and your council’s household waste recycling centre accepts lead-acid batteries — so ask before the old one ends up in a shed.

verdict: This is the one in its category with a real UK company behind it — Dynamic Battery Services Limited, Skelmersdale, trading since 1994 — and a four-year warranty on premium car batteries with a replacement-or-refund choice is a genuinely good offer. The mobility range looks the best value, with a 12v 7.2Ah at £20.50 delivered. Three things decide whether it suits you. Check the postcode list first: Northern Ireland, the Channel Islands and the Highlands and Islands are not served, and ten postcode areas carry £17.50 despite the “price you see is the price you pay” line. Buy the battery the Battery Finder recommends, and buy an AGM or EFB if your car has Stop-Start, because getting either wrong voids the warranty. And open the box the day it arrives — the terms give you seven days to report a problem even though the returns page says fourteen, and a late return attracts a 25% restocking fee. Get those right and it is a solid, well-priced British supplier.

faqs.q: How long is the warranty on a car battery?
faqs.a: Four years on the premium range and two years on the standard range. Mobility and leisure batteries carry one year, and batteries for taxis, forklifts and lawnmowers get twelve months. If the battery is faulty the site says you choose between a free replacement and a full refund.

faqs.q: What voids the warranty?
faqs.a: Two clauses matter most. Fitting a standard battery to a Stop-Start vehicle is excluded, so buy the AGM or EFB version if your engine switches off at the lights. And the battery must be the one the site’s Battery Finder recommended — overrule the tool and you are outside the cover. The usual exclusions also apply: wear and tear, over- or under-charging, sulphation, a charging-system fault on the car, failure to recover from a deep discharge, and flattening it by leaving the vehicle unused.

faqs.q: Does it deliver to my area?
faqs.a: Check before you order. Northern Ireland, the Channel Islands, the Highlands and Islands and the Outer Hebrides are excluded, and the site says delivery north of the Central Scottish Belt including Aberdeen is not possible. Separately, the postcode areas HS, IM, IV, KA, KW, PA, PH, TR, ZE and AB carry a £17.50 fee. Aberdeen sits in both lists on the same page, so ring and ask.

faqs.q: Can I get it tomorrow?
faqs.a: Probably not. Orders placed before 2pm on a weekday are dispatched the same day, but the delivery page states that only standard delivery is currently available because next-day consignments were being delayed — even though page titles and a FAQ badge elsewhere on the site still advertise next-day delivery. Saturday delivery is offered at an additional cost that is not published.

faqs.q: What does it cost to send a battery back?
faqs.a: If you are inside the window, the postage, which you pay unless the mistake was theirs. Outside it, anything they agree to take back is subject to a 25% restocking fee — about £30 on a £120 battery. Returns also need 24 hours’ notice before you send them, and non-faulty items left uncollected for three months are disposed of.

faqs.q: Will they take my old battery for recycling?
faqs.a: We could not find any take-back or recycling scheme published on the site. The Safety page deals with handling only and gives no disposal guidance, and nothing on the FAQ or terms pages covers it. That is what is missing from the website rather than a statement about what the company will do, so ask them. In the meantime a garage fitting a new battery will usually take the old one, and household waste recycling centres accept lead-acid batteries.

title: Three Business Mobiles
meta_title: Three Business Mobiles: The Prices They Do Not Show You
meta_description: Three's business SIM page shows no prices at all. Here are the published ex-VAT rates from its own price guide, from £11 a month, and the terms behind them.

headline.label: Cheapest business SIM
headline.value: £11 a month ex-VAT — 3GB, 24 months, unlimited minutes and texts

disclosure: we have no affiliate arrangement with Three and earn nothing if you sign up with them. The link on this page goes to Three’s own site. We list Three because it is one of the networks in this category, not because it pays us.
intro:
Three’s cheapest business SIM is £11 a month excluding VAT for 3GB on a 24-month term, with unlimited minutes and texts. Its most expensive is £29 for unlimited data on a one-month rolling term. There are fifteen plans in the grid, and not one of them has a price on Three’s business SIM page.

We checked all fifteen tiles. Every one shows “Contact us to buy” or “Buy now” and an “Increasing to:” field left blank. The only number on the page is a banner saying single SIMs start “from just £9 a month”, which does not correspond to any plan in the grid.

The prices do exist. They are in Three’s own Business Price Guide, a PDF effective 21 May 2026, and that is where every figure on this page comes from. If you are getting quotes, this is the table to have in front of you before you ring them.

sections.heading: The actual published prices, all excluding VAT
sections.html:
From Three’s Business Price Guide, for customers who joined, upgraded or added services on or after 1 December 2023. Unlimited minutes and texts on every plan.

Data1 month12 months24 months
3GB£18£12£11
25GB£23£16£14
80GB£26£20£15
500GB£28£22£19
Unlimited£29£24£22

Add 20% VAT if you cannot reclaim it: the 24-month unlimited plan is £22 ex-VAT and £26.40 inclusive. Three states plainly that “all prices in this Price Guide exclude VAT where applicable”, and it quotes its advertised savings the same way.

Two things about those figures are worth pausing on. The 1-month rate for 3GB is £18 against £11 on 24 months — you pay a 64% premium for flexibility on the smallest plan, which is the steepest flexibility penalty in the grid. And the jump from 80GB to 500GB on 24 months is £4, from £15 to £19, which makes the mid-tier plans poor value: 80GB costs £15 and more than six times the data costs £19.

The headline prices also include a £5 monthly discount for paying by a recurring method such as Direct Debit. Pay any other way and every figure above goes up by £5.

sections.heading: The annual rise is a fixed amount, and the band you land in matters
sections.html:
Three’s business contracts rise every April by a fixed amount rather than by an inflation index, and the amount depends on which price band your plan sits in. All figures exclude VAT:

  • Monthly charge of £9.99 or less — rises by £0.50
  • £10 to £20 — rises by £0.75
  • £20.01 and above — rises by £1.50

The bands create a cliff edge. A plan at £20.00 rises by 75p; a plan at £20.01 rises by £1.50, double the increase for one extra penny of monthly charge. Over a 24-month contract with two April rises, the difference is £18 per SIM.

Three Business Adapt and Dynamic are carved out of the fixed amounts and rise by 4.5% instead. Adapt is the route Three pushes businesses towards once you have 50 or more connections, so the larger you are, the more your increase tracks a percentage of a bigger bill.

sections.heading: The cancellation fee is harsher than the consumer one
sections.html:
This is the clause most worth knowing before signing, and it is a genuine difference between Three’s business and consumer contracts.

On a consumer contract, the fee for leaving early is the remaining monthly charges “less a variable discount, currently 3%”. Three’s own worked example: £25 a month with six months left is £150, minus £4.50, so £145.50.

On a business contract there is no such discount. The fee is “a lump sum equivalent to the total of the applicable Monthly Charges” remaining in the minimum term, and Three’s business worked example is the same £25 over six months at a flat £150. You pay the full remaining balance.

And it is charged per line. The price guide states that each SIM may carry its own cancellation fee. On a fleet of ten SIMs at £22 a month with a year left, that is £2,640 ex-VAT to walk away. Price the exit before you price the plan.

sections.heading: Shared data across the account, and the add-on nobody can read
sections.html:
Three’s most useful business feature is account-level shared data. You buy an allowance at billing-account level and it applies to every connection under that account, whatever individual plan each line is on. Sizes run from 30GB to 50TB.

The prices are published as two lists — one-off add-ons at £24, £80, £200, £400 and £760, and recurring ones at £21, £70, £175, £350 and £665. What is not published is which price buys which allowance. The table’s columns do not line up in Three’s own PDF, and the guide itself tells you to ring 337 to find out.

One important restriction: “recurring add-on allowances cannot be rolled over”. Unused shared data does not carry into the next month, so buying headroom for a busy quarter means paying for it in the quiet ones too.

Out of allowance, business data is 1p per MB ex-VAT, which works out at roughly £10 a GB. A single employee tethering a laptop for an afternoon can clear the price of their whole monthly plan.

sections.heading: Is the network actually any good? Ofcom's own answer
sections.html:
Three makes two claims on its business pages — “UK’s Fastest 5G Network” and “award-winning” — and publishes no basis for either on the page itself. Ofcom’s own measurement is more useful, and it is good news for Three.

In Ofcom’s Mobile Matters 2025, published 17 July 2025 on data to March 2025:

  • “Three’s download speeds tended to be faster than the other MNOs’ on 5G.”
  • 10MB file download times over 5G ranged from 0.8 seconds for Three to 1.4 seconds for EE — Three was fastest.
  • Three had the highest share of 5G connections at 50 Mbit/s or above, at 75%.
  • Three had the best 5G latency, with operator averages spanning 15 to 21 milliseconds.

On complaints, Ofcom’s Q1 2026 figures put Three at 2 complaints per 100,000 pay-monthly subscribers — exactly the industry average, level with Tesco Mobile, better than Sky Mobile on 4 and O2 and iD Mobile on 3, behind EE, Giffgaff and Vodafone on 1 each.

Coverage, in Three’s own words: the combined 4G and 5G network covers 99% of the outdoor population, with 4,700 5G sites across 650 towns and cities. Three has switched off its 3G network entirely, so older handsets and some payment terminals will not fall back to it. Ofcom’s Connected Nations 2025 adds one qualifier worth knowing: “Three does not currently deploy 5G SA services” — standalone 5G.

sections.heading: Where it falls short for a business buyer
sections.html:
You cannot shop without talking to someone. Fifteen plan tiles, no prices, “Contact us to buy”. For a small business comparing three networks on a Tuesday afternoon, that is a real cost in time, and it is a choice Three has made rather than a technical limitation — the prices are published in a PDF two clicks away.

No published limit on connections, in either direction. We could find no stated minimum or maximum in the business terms or the price guide. The multibuy discount covers “up to 9 SIMs”, teams of 50+ get routed to Three Business Adapt, and Three Mobile Protect “covers up to 25 devices” — but none of those is a contractual limit on how many lines you can hold.

No international calling bundle is published at all. For a business making regular overseas calls that is a significant gap in the published information; the pages link to “Calling abroad” without naming a product or a price.

Device management is listed without detail. Three Device Management, Three Mobile Protect and Three Analyst all appear as names with no pricing and no specification, and Mobile Protect stops at 25 devices, beyond which it is “a separate service” that is also unpriced.

One advertised price does not add up. Three’s business homepage shows an unlimited data SIM at “£17 a month, rising to £17.75 from April 2026 and £28.50 from April 2027”. A £10.75 step in year two is seven times the published £1.50 band increase, so it is almost certainly a promotional price expiring rather than an annual rise — but Three presents it as the rise. Read any Three business quote for the year-two and year-three numbers, not just the headline.

sections.heading: Who owns Three now, and why it matters to a business contract
sections.html:
The company you contract with is Hutchison 3G UK Limited, company number 03885486, registered at 450 Longwater Avenue, Green Park, Reading RG2 6GF, incorporated 29 November 1999.

It is no longer independent. Three’s merger with Vodafone completed on 31 May 2025, creating VodafoneThree, initially 51% Vodafone and 49% CK Hutchison. On 5 May 2026 Vodafone agreed to buy out the remaining 49% for £4.3 billion, with completion expected in the second half of 2026 subject to National Security and Investment Act approval. Vodafone says there will be “no change to VodafoneThree’s multi-brand strategy”, so Three continues to sell as Three.

For a business signing a 24-month contract, the relevant detail is that the CMA cleared the merger on 5 December 2024 subject to legally binding commitments, with final undertakings accepted on 28 March 2025. The network must be built out over eight years from completion, and Ofcom has primary responsibility for monitoring it, with quarterly meetings for the duration. VodafoneThree has committed £11 billion of investment — a figure it states itself, over “the next 10 years” in one place and “by 2034” in another. The CMA’s own undertakings say only “invest billions”, so treat £11bn as the company’s commitment rather than a regulator-enforced one.
